title: fix(workbench): stop asserting exact username on homepage login check (closes #273)
description:
## Summary

- The `test_workbench_login` step `the current user is shown in the header` was using `to_have_text(test_username)` against `#current-user`. On the new Workbench homepage, that element shows the user's **display name** (e.g. `Shane Halloran`), not the login username (e.g. `shaneh02`), causing false failures.
- Changed the assertion to `to_be_visible()` + `not_to_be_empty()`. Reaching the homepage already proves login succeeded; we don't need to exact-match which text appears.
- Updated the `.feature` step wording to truthfully describe the new assertion.

Closes #273

## Legacy homepage caveat

Per issue comment from @samcofer: this test may behave differently if the test user is still on the **legacy homepage** (pre-new-UI). The fix does not attempt to handle the legacy case — if someone encounters this, the visible/non-empty assertion should still pass as long as `#current-user` exists, but we do not guard against a structurally different legacy page. Consider surfacing a warning if the legacy homepage is detected.

## Demo

# fix(workbench): stop asserting exact username on homepage login check

*2026-06-11T16:00:04Z by Showboat 0.6.1*

The Workbench new homepage shows the user's display name (e.g. 'Shane Halloran') in the #current-user element rather than the login username (e.g. 'shaneh02'). The old assertion used to_have_text(test_username) which failed whenever the display name differed from the login ID.

The fix (issue #273 option 3): assert the #current-user element is visible and non-empty. Reaching the homepage already proves login succeeded -- we do not need to verify which specific text appears.

Note from issue commenter: this test can fail on legacy homepages (users who have not switched to the new homepage). The fix does not attempt to support the legacy homepage; if a test user is on the legacy homepage the visible/non-empty assertion should still pass as long as the element exists, but the surrounding page structure may differ.

title: fix(ssl): accept HTTPS termination behind load balancers in redirect test (closes #265)
description:
## Summary

- Accept HTTPS termination behind AWS ALB (and other load balancers) in the SSL redirect test
- The existing 3xx → `https://` Location check is preserved as the primary path
- Added fallback: follow redirects and pass if the final URL scheme is `https`
- Closes #265

## Demo

# Fix: HTTPS redirect test accepts ALB termination

*2026-06-11T15:59:56Z by Showboat 0.6.1*

The SSL redirect test previously only accepted a direct 3xx response with an https:// Location header. Behind an AWS ALB (or similar load balancer), the HTTP→HTTPS upgrade can happen transparently — the client may receive a 200 after the ALB internally redirects, or the redirect chain may differ from a plain 3xx. This caused false failures even when HTTP traffic correctly ended up at HTTPS (confirmed in a browser). The fix adds a fallback: follow the redirect chain (follow_redirects=True) and pass if the final URL scheme is https. The primary 3xx path is preserved so direct-redirect deployments still pass as before.

Release notes

Sourced from astral-sh/setup-uv's releases.

v8.2.0 🌈 New inputs quiet and download-from-astral-mirror

Changes

This release brings two new inputs and a few bug fixes.

New inputs

Lets talk about the new inputs first.

quiet

Pretty simple. It turns of all info loggings. Useful if you use this in a composite action and are not interested in all the details. In the upcoming releases we will add log groups to fully implement support for "less noise"

[!NOTE]
Warnings and errors are always logged.

download-from-astral-mirror

In some cases you may want to directly use the fallback of checking for available versions and downloading releases from GitHub instead of using the astral.sh mirror. Setting download-from-astral-mirror: false allows you to do that.

Bugfixes

When using the astral.sh mirror to query available versions and download releases (done by default) we now stop sending the GitHub token in the header. The mirror never looked at it but we shouldn't be handing out that data even if it is just a short lived token. All other bugfixes try to limit the impact of failed GitHub queries due to retries and other faults.

We couldn't pinpoint all rootcauses yet but added more logging for error cases to track them down.

title: ci: fix stale preview-screenshot lockfile and guard against drift
description:
**Fix #347.** The `Capture preview screenshots` workflow failed on every run: the agent job is skipped with *"Stale lock file check failed"*, then a failure issue is auto-filed (consolidating #282/#319/#333).

Root cause: a dependabot action-group bump (#340) edited `preview-screenshot-gallery.lock.yml`'s action pins (incl. `gh-aw-actions/setup` → v0.77.0) **without recompiling**, so the committed lockfile no longer matched what the runtime produces, and it was missing the network-allowlist domains from #326.

**Changes:**
- Recompiled `preview-screenshot-gallery.lock.yml` with `gh aw compile` (v0.74.8) — re-pins setup to v0.74.8 (consistent with the other two workflows) and restores the google-fonts/jsdelivr domains. No `.md` change.
- Added an **Agentic Workflow Lockfile Guard** CI job that recompiles and fails on any `.lock.yml` drift — catching this class of staleness in PR CI instead of at runtime.
- Added `actions/create-github-app-token` to the dependabot ignore (it's only used inside the gh-aw lockfiles). `gh-aw-actions/**` was already ignored.

Note: the 5 other shared actions can't be dependabot-ignored (they're used in real workflows too), which is exactly why the CI guard is the durable fix.

Closes #347

title: ci: fix gh-aw bash allowlists to permit command arguments
description:
The agentic-workflow agents could not run any `uv run` / `just` / `pytest` command — every call was denied with *"Permission denied and could not request permission from user"* (issue #354, and the cause of the broken impl PR #353).

Root cause: the bash allowlists used the `"uv run *"` (space-star) form, which gh-aw compiles to `shell(uv run)` — matching only the bare command with **no arguments**. The correct form is `"uv run:*"` (colon-star), which compiles to `shell(uv run:*)` and permits arguments (the same form gh-aw auto-injects for `git add:*` etc.).

Applies the colon-star fix to both `implement-plan.md` and `issue-triage.md` and recompiles both lockfiles. Verified: the lockfiles now emit `shell(uv run:*)`, `shell(just:*)`, `shell(uvx showboat:*)`, etc.

`preview-screenshot-gallery.md` has no bash allowlist, so it is unaffected — its #347 failures are a separate engine/infra cause.

Closes #354

title: fix(plugin): preserve line breaks in error_summary (closes #344)
description:
Closes #344

Implements the plan from #345

## Summary

`failures.json`'s `error_summary` field was flattened to a single line even when the underlying exception contained structured multi-line output (e.g. `--- Task output ---` blobs from Connect deployments). This made the field much harder to read than the `feature` field, which preserves its newlines.

### Changes

**`src/vip/plugin.py`**
- `_extract_exception_info`: join E-line continuations with `"\n"` instead of `" "`, so multi-line exception messages survive into `concise_error` and ultimately `failures.json`.
- `pytest_runtest_logreport` terminal call site: flatten `exc_message` with `.replace("\n", " ")` before passing to `_format_concise_error`, so the `FAILED` summary line in pytest's terminal output stays single-line.

**`selftests/test_plugin.py`**
- `test_failures_json_uses_concise_error`: replaced the `< 200` character-count assertion with a format-validity check (multi-line summaries may legitimately exceed 200 chars).
- Added `test_error_summary_preserves_line_breaks`: raises a `RuntimeError` with embedded newlines and asserts `failures.json` retains them.
- Added `test_terminal_failed_line_stays_single_line`: same fixture, asserts the terminal `FAILED` line does not contain embedded newlines.

## Demo

The `uv`/`uvx` toolchain was unavailable in the implementation runner, so the `showboat` workflow could not be executed. CI will verify lint and selftests. See `validation_docs/demo-bot-implement-issue-344.md` for the change summary.

### Core change (plugin.py)

```python
# Before — flattens multi-line error to one line:
return m.group(1), " ".join(line for line in msg_lines if line)

# After — preserves newlines in error_summary:
return m.group(1), "\n".join(line for line in msg_lines if line)
```

```python
# Terminal display site — flatten only for the FAILED line:
report.longrepr = _format_concise_error(report.nodeid, exc_type, exc_message.replace("\n", " "))
```

title: ci: make issue triage opt-in and add issue lifecycle labels
description:
Reworks the bot triage pipeline around a human checkpoint at the front and visible issue state throughout.

**Opt-in triage** (`issue-triage.md`): the agent no longer fires on every newly opened issue. It triggers only when a maintainer applies the `needs-bot-triage` label, and removes the label on pickup (re-apply to re-run). Replaces the old `re-triage` label.

**Issue lifecycle labels:** an issue's labels now show where it is — `needs-bot-triage` (opt-in) → `triaged-by-bot` + `plan-pending-review` (plan PR awaiting review) → `implementing` (plan merged, impl PR in flight) → closed on merge. `implement-plan.md` gained `add-labels`/`remove-labels` outputs (with `target: "*"`) to swap the label on the originating issue and comment there as implementation starts.

**Implement-run resilience** (`implement-plan.md`): `timeout-minutes` raised 20 → 30, plus instructions to ship the smallest coherent slice, commit incrementally, and open a draft PR with a remaining-work checklist instead of producing nothing on timeout (as run 27211949474 did).

Lock files recompiled with `gh aw compile` (v0.74.8); zizmor clean. Docs updated (`docs/agentic-workflows.md`, `AGENTS.md`).

title: ci: guard against stray uv.lock changes in PRs
description:
Bot-generated plan/docs PRs have repeatedly carried a stale `uv.lock` from an old base. It is invisible until it fails the Dependency Audit (vulnerable transitive pins on #309/#317/#346) or conflicts with `main` on merge (#309). A real dependency change always touches `pyproject.toml`, so a lone `uv.lock` change is the drift signal.

Adds a `Lockfile Guard` job: PRs that modify `uv.lock` without `pyproject.toml` fail with instructions to restore the lockfile. Legit dependency bumps (which touch both) and code/docs PRs are unaffected.

Note: the duplicate-module defect from #349 is already caught by ruff F811 in `Lint & Format`, so no separate check is added here.

title: feat(workbench): add in-session execution primitives (closes #301)
description:
Closes #301
Implements the plan from #317

## Summary

Adds marker-bracketed in-session execution primitives for Workbench IDE tests. All helpers wrap the caller's expression with a unique UUID sentinel so its output can be reliably extracted from accumulated console scrollback — distinguishing this command's output from prior history and knowing when execution is complete.

### Architecture

Follows the four-layer architecture: `exec.py` is Layer 2 (DSL), delegating to existing page-object selectors (Layer 3) and Playwright (Layer 4). Pure logic helpers are fully unit-tested without requiring Playwright or a live Workbench deployment.

### Changes

**New: `src/vip_tests/workbench/exec.py`**
- `rstudio_eval(page, expr, timeout)` — R in the RStudio console
- `positron_eval_r(page, expr, timeout)` — R in the Positron console  
- `positron_eval_python(page, expr, timeout)` — Python in the Positron console
- `jupyterlab_eval(page, expr, lang, timeout)` — notebook cell (Python or R kernel)
- `vscode_eval(page, expr, lang, timeout)` — VS Code Python/R REPL output panel
- `terminal_run(page, cmd, timeout)` — terminal redirect + DOM-rendered file readback (no xterm canvas scraping)
- `file_exists(page, path, timeout)` — server-side path check via console expression
- `read_file(page, path, timeout)` — server-side file contents via console expression
- Pure helpers: `_wrap_r_expr`, `_wrap_python_expr`, `_extract_between_markers`, `_strip_r_index`, `_make_sentinels`

**Modified: `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_ide_launch.py`**
- Refactored `rstudio_executes_r_code` step to delegate to `exec.rstudio_eval`, preserving test behavior but using the shared primitive

**Modified: `src/vip_tests/workbench/pages/positron_session.py`**
- Added `CONSOLE_INPUT` selector for the Positron console Monaco editor textarea

**Modified: `src/vip_tests/workbench/pages/vscode_session.py`**
- Added `REPL_INPUT` and `REPL_OUTPUT` selectors for the VS Code Python/R Interactive Window

**Modified: `src/vip/config.py`**
- Added optional `test_packages: list[str]` field to `WorkbenchConfig` for package-install scenarios (e.g. `["sf", "DBI", "Matrix"]`)

**New: `selftests/test_workbench_exec.py`**
- 34 selftests covering all pure-logic helpers without Playwright

**Modified: `selftests/test_config.py`**
- 4 new tests for `WorkbenchConfig.test_packages`

### Terminal execution design

`terminal_run` avoids xterm canvas/WebGL scraping entirely: it redirects stdout/stderr to a unique temp file and appends a done sentinel, then polls for the sentinel via DOM-rendered file readback (`read_file`). This makes terminal execution a committed capability, not a spike.

### Future work (enabled by this PR, out of scope)

- `test_package_install.feature/.py` — install R/Python packages from PPM
- `test_document_rendering.feature/.py` — knit RMarkdown, render Quarto docs  
- `test_database_connectivity.feature/.py` — DBI/odbc/SQLAlchemy queries

## Demo

See `validation_docs/demo-bot-implement-issue-301.md` for the full selftest and lint results.

### New config option

```toml
[workbench]
test_packages = ["sf", "DBI", "Matrix"]  # packages for install-verification scenarios
```

### Key primitive usage example

```python
from vip_tests.workbench.exec import rstudio_eval

# In a step definition:
result = rstudio_eval(page, "packageVersion('Matrix')")
assert "1." in result
```

title: docs: plan for #344 — preserve line breaks in error_summary
description:
Closes #344.

This PR adds a plan for preserving line breaks in the `error_summary` field of `failures.json` so it is as readable as the `feature` field.

**Summary of the proposed change**

The root cause lives in `src/vip/plugin.py::_extract_exception_info`: continuation `E   ...` lines are joined with a single space, flattening any meaningful line structure (e.g. `--- Task output ---` blocks) before the value reaches `concise_error` and ultimately `failures.json`'s `error_summary`. The plan calls for joining with `\n` instead, while collapsing newlines back to spaces only at the terminal-display call site so pytest's `FAILED ...` line stays compact. New selftests in `selftests/test_plugin.py` will assert that multi-line messages survive into `failures.json` and that the terminal output does not regress.

The full plan, including architecture, components, verification steps, open questions, and out-of-scope items, lives in `thoughts/shared/plans/2026-06-05-issue-344-error-summary-line-breaks.md`.

Merging this PR will trigger an implementation PR — comment to iterate on the plan first.

title: ci: smoke test updates, including running against the latest version
description:
## Summary

As we are having some internal tests against different envs, and because we were missing when these tests were failing, I've made some updates to how they work.  This also fixes a problem with Workbench tests that showed up when these were run.

This PR makes the product smoke tests (Connect, Workbench, Package Manager) exercise the **latest** product version, changes **when** they run so they fire on relevant PRs/pushes (with daily coverage moving to team-notified runs), and includes the two fixes needed to get the latest-version smoke tests green in CI.

## 1. Test the latest version

The smoke tests were pinned to stale versions. They now resolve the latest stable build on every run.

| Workflow | Before (push/PR) | After (push/PR) |
|---|---|---|
| **Workbench** | `["2026.01.1"]` (~4mo stale) | `["release"]` |
| **Connect** | `["2024.08.0", "release"]` | `["release"]` |
| **Package Manager** | `["ubuntu2204-2024.08.0"]` (~2yr stale) | `["ubuntu2204"]` |

`release` / `ubuntu2204` (unversioned) always resolve to the latest stable build. The stale `2024.08.0` baselines are dropped.

## 2. When the smoke tests run

- **Path-filtered triggers:** `push` (to `main`) and `pull_request` now only trigger a product's smoke workflow when files that could affect the result change — `src/**`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, or that workflow file itself. Docs-only and unrelated changes no longer spend CI on full product smoke runs.
- **Daily cron removed:** the in-repo `schedule:` (daily) triggers are removed from all three workflows. Scheduled coverage moves to team-created daily runs that notify each owning team, so failures are surfaced to the right people instead of on every PR.

## 3. Fixes needed to go green against latest

- **`fix(deps)`** — bump `pip` to `>=26.1.2` for advisory `PYSEC-2026-196`, which the Dependency Audit (`pip-audit`) job flagged on `pip` 26.1.1 (`pip` is transitive via `pip-api`/`pip-audit`).
- **`fix(workbench)`** — Workbench 2026.05.0 renders the homepage Quit button as `"Quit (N)"` instead of plain `"Quit"`, which broke the IDE-launch smoke tests at the session-cleanup step. The prior `:text-matches('^Quit( \(\d+\))?$')` regex selector silently matched **zero** buttons because Playwright's selector parser strips one level of backslash escaping inside the quoted argument, mangling the regex. Replaced it with a regex-free, backward-compatible selector — `button:text-is('Quit'), button:has-text('Quit (')` — that matches both the old `"Quit"` and the new `"Quit (N)"` while excluding the separate `"Quit All"` button.

## Trade-off

Tracking the moving `release` / `ubuntu2204` tags means the exact resolved version can change between runs (not perfectly reproducible), in exchange for never drifting stale. Each job title and report still surfaces the resolved version for traceability.

## Verification

Smoke tests run only in CI (Docker products + license secrets). On this branch all three smoke workflows pass against the latest versions (Workbench resolved to 2026.05.0: `6 passed, 2 skipped`), and the Dependency Audit, selftests, lint, type-check, and build checks are all green.

## Demo

See `validation_docs/demo-workbench-quit-button-versioned.md` for a reproducible before/after of the Quit-button selector fix.

Updates `htmltools` from 0.6.1 to 0.7.0
Release notes

Sourced from htmltools's releases.

htmltools 0.7.0

Breaking changes

  • Tagifiable.tagify()'s return annotation is now Tagified, a new type alias for the union of fully-tagified shapes (TagifiedNode | float | None | Sequence[Tagified], mirroring TagChild). Custom .tagify() implementations annotated with bare TagList / Tag return types should switch to -> Tagified, or drop the annotation. Runtime behavior of correct implementations is unchanged. (#105, #116)

  • The result of .tagify() is now immutable. Calling .append, .extend, .insert, .add_class, __setitem__, or the context-manager with form on a tagified value raises AttributeError and is a static type error. Mutate on the buildable Tag / TagList side, then call .tagify() once to produce the render-ready result. (#116)

  • TagList.tagify() now raises TypeError at the boundary when a child's .tagify() returns un-tagified content (e.g. a bare TagList containing a still-Tagifiable object). The error names the offending class and slot index so buggy .tagify() implementations surface at the source. The render-time RuntimeError for the same family of violations has been clarified. (#7, #105, #112, #116)

New features

  • Exported the new tagified sibling classes TagifiedTag and TagifiedTagList. Use them in narrow annotations (def f(t: TagifiedTag): ...) and isinstance checks on .tagify() output. (#116)

  • Added is_tagified(x) for runtime distinguishability between buildable Tag / TagList and their tagified counterparts. Returns a TypeIs[...] so pyright narrows at call sites. (#116)

Dependencies

  • Bumped typing-extensions floor to >=4.12.0.

Other changes

  • Switched the contributor workflow to uv and reorganized Makefile targets. Run make setup (or make ai-setup) to bootstrap a dev environment, and make help to list available targets. pip install -e ".[dev,test]" no longer works since dev and test are now PEP 735 dependency groups; use uv sync --all-groups instead. (#107)

  • Replaced black, isort, and flake8 with ruff for linting and formatting. Run make format to auto-fix, or make check-format to verify. (#110)

title: ci: add path filters to ci, preview, and website-preview workflows
description:
## Summary

- `ci.yml` — lint, typecheck, and selftests now only run on PRs that touch `src/`, `selftests/`, `examples/`, `docker/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, or the CI config itself; push to `main` stays unfiltered
- `preview.yml` — report preview build now only triggers when `report/`, `src/`, `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`, or the workflow files change
- `website-preview.yml` — website preview build now mirrors the same path list as `website.yml` (which was already scoped), skipping runs for PRs that only touch unrelated files

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a PR that only touches docs or a `thoughts/` file — confirm `CI`, `Report Preview`, and `Website Preview` do not trigger
- [ ] Open a PR that touches `src/` — confirm all three trigger normally
- [ ] Open a PR that touches `website/` — confirm `Website Preview` triggers but `CI` and `Report Preview` do not
- [ ] Confirm preview cleanup still fires when a PR with relevant changes is closed

title: feat(workbench): add Background Job and Workbench Job test coverage (closes #302)
description:
Closes #302
Implements the plan from #316

## Summary

Adds BDD test coverage for Workbench Background Jobs and Workbench Jobs (Launcher jobs) in RStudio Pro sessions — the gap identified in issue #302.

### What changed

- **`src/vip_tests/workbench/test_jobs.feature`** — two new `@workbench` scenarios:
  - *Background Job runs and completes* — submits an inline R script via the Background Jobs pane and verifies it produces expected output
  - *Workbench Job runs and completes* — submits the same script as a Launcher job via the Workbench Jobs pane
- **`src/vip_tests/workbench/test_jobs.py`** — Playwright step definitions following the four-layer architecture; defensive `pytest.skip` guards when either Jobs UI is absent in the deployment
- **`src/vip_tests/workbench/pages/rstudio_session.py`** — job-related selectors for Background Jobs and Workbench Jobs panes added to `RStudioSession`
- **`src/vip/config.py`** — `job_timeout` field added to `WorkbenchConfig` (default 120 s); configurable via `[workbench] job_timeout` in vip.toml so operators can adapt to slow clusters without code changes
- **`selftests/test_config.py`** — three tests covering `job_timeout` default, explicit value, and from-dict round-trip

### Config option

```toml
[workbench]
job_timeout = 300  # seconds (default: 120)
```

title: feat(workbench): add Kubernetes autoscaling and capacity probes (closes #304)
description:
Closes #304

Implements the plan from #311

## What changed and why

This PR adds Kubernetes-specific session capacity and autoscaling tests to VIP's Workbench test suite, as requested in #304. A Posit customer running Kubernetes-backed Workbench flagged six scenarios around autoscaling boundaries, capacity limits, and resource profile enforcement that weren't covered by the existing `test_session_capacity.feature`.

### New files

**`src/vip/clients/kubernetes.py`**
Read-only `KubernetesClient` using the `kubernetes` Python SDK. Credentials are inherited from the ambient environment (`~/.kube/config`, `KUBECONFIG` env var, or in-cluster service account) — no separate credential fields in `vip.toml`. The SDK import is lazy: if the package isn't installed, a `RuntimeError` with a clear install hint is raised, and the corresponding test scenarios skip via `pytest.skip`.

**`src/vip_tests/workbench/test_session_capacity_k8s.feature`**
Six Gherkin scenarios with the `@workbench` tag:
1. Autoscaler adds a node when sessions fill current capacity
2. New session lands on a node after scale-up
3. Session count respects the configured maximum
4. Sessions launched in quick succession all reach Active state
5. Session is routed to the expected node pool for the resource profile
6. Resource profile enforces CPU and memory limits

**`src/vip_tests/workbench/test_session_capacity_k8s.py`**
Step definitions for all six scenarios. Every scenario that needs cluster config gates on `@given("the Kubernetes cluster is configured")`, which skips cleanly when `[workbench.kubernetes]` is absent or `enabled = false`.

**`selftests/test_workbench_kubernetes_config.py`**
Config-layer selftests covering `WorkbenchKubernetesConfig` defaults, `from_dict`, `load_config` integration with a real TOML file, and the `repr` of `WorkbenchConfig`.

### Modified files

**`src/vip/config.py`**
Adds `WorkbenchKubernetesConfig` dataclass with fields: `enabled`, `namespace`, `node_pool_profiles` (pool→profile mapping), `max_sessions`, `profile_cpu_limit`, `profile_memory_limit_gib`. Wired into `WorkbenchConfig.from_dict` under the `[workbench.kubernetes]` TOML key.

**`src/vip_tests/workbench/conftest.py`**
The shared `@given("Workbench is accessible and I am logged in")` step was moved here from `test_session_capacity.py` so both capacity feature files use it without duplicate step registration.

**`src/vip_tests/conftest.py`**
Adds a `kubernetes_client` session fixture (returns `None` when K8s is not configured).

**`vip.toml.example`**
Documents the new `[workbench.kubernetes]` block with all fields commented out.

## Scope guards

All new scenarios skip when:
- `[workbench.kubernetes]` is absent or `enabled = false`
- The `kubernetes` Python package is not installed
- A specific sub-config (e.g., `node_pool_profiles`, `max_sessions`) required by a scenario is not set

## Out of scope (per plan)

- No cluster mutation — VIP remains a read-only observer
- Non-Kubernetes launchers not covered
- Autoscaler installation/configuration not handled
- Performance benchmarking excluded

title: docs: plan for #288 — improved timeout configuration
description:
Closes part of #288 (planning step).

This PR proposes a plan for issue #288: a single `VIP_TIMEOUT_SCALE` environment-variable multiplier that scales every genuine operation timeout in VIP uniformly. Merging triggers the implementation PR.

## Design

**One env var, applied at constant-definition time.**

```
VIP_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3 vip verify --connect-url https://connect.example.com …
```

A new dependency-free leaf module (`src/vip/timeouts.py`) exports `timeout_scale()` and `scaled(value)`. Because `VIP_TIMEOUT_SCALE` is readable at module-import time, it can reach constants that a TOML-config or pytest-fixture approach cannot — specifically the seven module-level Playwright constants in `src/vip_tests/workbench/conftest.py` (`TIMEOUT_SESSION_START = 90_000`, etc.) that are imported by 9 step files at load time, before any fixture exists. That is the root reason the design is env-var-only.

**What gets scaled:**
- All 7 Playwright constants in `src/vip_tests/workbench/conftest.py` (scaled at definition, so all 9 importing step files pick it up with no call-site changes)
- IdP login-form and network-idle waits in `src/vip/idp.py`
- Browser-click and page-load waits in `src/vip/auth.py` (operation timeouts only)
- `BaseClient.__init__` default (30 s) via None-sentinel — constructors in `connect.py`, `workbench.py`, `packagemanager.py` pass through; callers that supply an explicit value opt out
- `wait_for_task` and `wait_for_system_check` defaults in `src/vip/clients/connect.py`
- `--timeout` k8s job flag default (900 s, `cli.py:1228`/`1230`); the None-sentinel pattern means `args.timeout - 60` fed to `job.py:56` (`timeout_seconds: int = 840`) and the polling budget in `stream_logs`/`wait_for_job` all propagate correctly
- Two `httpx.Client(timeout=30.0)` instances in `src/vip/verify/credentials.py` that bypass `BaseClient`
- Hardcoded `wait_for_task(timeout=300)` literals in `src/vip_tests/connect/test_packages.py:93` and `src/vip_tests/cross_product/test_integration.py:48`

**What is deliberately NOT scaled:**
- `idp.py:_MFA_TIMEOUT` (5-minute window) — this is a human wait, not a server operation
- All `page.wait_for_timeout(500)` / `wait_for_timeout(1000)` busy-loop pacing sleeps — scaling poll intervals only slows the loop on fast machines without preventing any timeout
- The existing per-section absolute knobs (`[connect].deploy_timeout`, `[workbench].job_timeout`, `[performance].page_load_timeout`) — these stay unchanged; the scale multiplies on top of whatever effective value is in play
- Values <1.0 are valid (scale down for CI speed checks)

**Why not `vip.toml`:** TOML is parsed after module load. The Playwright/IdP constants must be evaluated at import time. An env var is the only mechanism that satisfies that constraint without a separate module-reload pass.

## Open questions

None. The earlier draft's open questions (env vs. file precedence, MFA exclusion, legacy-knob deprecation) are all resolved in the plan's design rationale.

- Fixes #288

title: fix(issue-triage): allow cd and unmask re-triage label removal
description:
The triage bot has never actually removed the `re-triage` label. Both #293 (conditional) and #300 (unconditional `|| true`) failed for the same hidden reason, found by inspecting a live run (#288, run 26783177062):

- The agent wrapped the removal in `cd /home/runner/work/vip/vip && gh issue edit … --remove-label re-triage`.
- The Copilot CLI tool-gate denied the compound command because `cd` was not in the bash allow-list (only `gh issue edit` was), logging "Permission denied and could not request permission from user".
- The trailing `|| true` then forced exit 0, so the run reported success while the label silently persisted.

## Fix

- Add `cd *` to the bash allow-list so the agent's `cd && gh issue edit` compound is permitted.
- Drop `|| true` so a future denial or API failure is visible in the run log instead of swallowed.
- Gate the removal on `re-triage` actually being present (the agent has the labels from Step 1), so it does not error on fresh `opened` issues.
- Also instruct the agent to run the command bare (no `cd` prefix) as a second line of defense.

Compiled lock now contains `shell(cd)`. Must merge to main before validating — the workflow runs from the default branch for issue events, not from PR branches. Will re-validate on #288 after merge.

title: fix(connect): stop data-source step being collected as a stray test
description:
## Summary

`uv run vip verify --package-manager-url ...` errored out with a **Connect** test running during a Package-Manager-only run:

```
ERROR at setup of test_connectivity
test_connectivity: an unexpected error occurred: ValueError: connect_client did not yield a value
```

### Root cause

The Connect `@when` step for *"I test connectivity to each data source"* was named **`test_connectivity`** (`src/vip_tests/connect/test_data_sources.py`). Because that matches pytest's default `python_functions = test_*` pattern, pytest collected it as a **standalone test** in addition to registering it as a pytest-bdd step.

The stray test carried none of the feature file's `@connect` marker (that marker is applied only to the `@scenario` function), so the plugin's product deselection in `_should_deselect_for_product` never excluded it. During a Package-Manager-only run it executed anyway, where the Connect dir's autouse cleanup fixtures pull in the `connect_client` fixture — which `return`s (instead of `yield`s) when Connect is unconfigured, raising `connect_client did not yield a value`.

It was the only step function in the suite named `test_*`; every other `def test_*` is a legitimate `@scenario` function.

### Changes

- Rename the step to `check_connectivity_to_each_data_source`. The function name is arbitrary (the step is matched by its Gherkin string and exposes state via `target_fixture="ds_results"`), so this is a surgical change.
- Add `selftests/test_step_naming.py`, which scans every step file and fails if any `@given`/`@when`/`@then` function is named `test_*` — preventing this whole class of bug going forward.

### Verification

- New regression test fails on the old name, passes after the rename.
- With a Package-Manager-only config, `test_data_sources.py` now collects `1 item / 1 deselected / 0 selected` (only the scenario, deselected) — the stray test is gone.
- Full selftest suite: 607 passed, 3 skipped. `just check` clean.

## Demo

title: feat: support Snowflake OAuth for Posit Team Native Apps
description:
> Draft — supports rstudio/partnership-snowflake#3022. Opening for review/visibility.

Adds the auth plumbing VIP needs to verify **Posit Team deployed as a Snowflake Native App**, plus the per-request-auth fixes that surface once products are reached through the SPCS ingress.

## 1. Browser auth — Snowflake IdP strategy
`idp.py` gains `_fill_snowflake_login`, registered as `idp = "snowflake"`. Posit Team products delegate OIDC to the deployment's **controller**, which itself sits behind the Snowpark Container Services ingress — so reaching a product bounces through Snowflake OAuth more than once (product-host ingress, then controller host). The strategy loops, filling each sign-in form in the chain (waiting for each hop to settle) and clicking the optional **Allow** consent, until the flow leaves Snowflake.

## 2. HTTP client auth — pluggable seam
Snowflake's SPCS ingress expects a per-host `Authorization: Snowflake Token="…"` (a key-pair JWT exchange), which a static API key can't express. Rather than teach VIP about Snowflake, this adds a small generic seam:
- `client_auth.py`: `register_client_auth(idp, factory)` / `build_client_auth(...)`.
- An optional `auth: httpx.Auth` on `BaseClient` and the product clients, plus a `BaseClient.auth` accessor.
- Client fixtures consult the registry and skip the Connect API-key requirement when a provider is registered.

A downstream extension (in `partnership-snowflake`) registers a Snowflake `httpx.Auth` against `idp="snowflake"`; VIP stays Snowflake-agnostic.

## 3. Auth that survives the ingress
The SPCS ingress owns the `Authorization` header, so any product credential carried there is clobbered — and any ad-hoc HTTP call that skips the product client carries no auth at all and gets 302'd to the ingress OAuth login.
- **Connect** — the API key moves to `X-RSC-Authorization` (honored by Connect universally) so it coexists with the ingress token; `fetch_content` now passes `auth` so deployed content is reachable.
- **Performance category** — the suite issued bare `httpx.get()` calls (package install speed, resource-usage load + `/metrics`, concurrency, login load times) that bypassed the clients and so carried no auth: status-asserting tests failed and latency-only tests *falsely passed* by timing the redirect. All call sites now thread the client auth (via `BaseClient.auth` or `build_client_auth(...)`). Null-safe: non-Snowflake deployments get `auth=None`, a no-op.

## Validated live (Snowflake posit-team deployment)
- **Workbench** — API/security/health (JWT prong) + UI subset (serial; concurrency limit, not auth).
- **Connect** — double-bounce login + content deploy/build/serve via `X-RSC-Authorization`.
- **Package Manager** — repo/mirror tests pass; performance tests pass post-fix. (`test_prometheus_metrics` reaches PM but 404s — PM serves metrics on an internal port, not the public ingress; candidate for `@if_applicable`.)

## Tests
`selftests/test_idp.py`, `selftests/test_client_auth.py`; selftest suite green, ruff + mypy clean. No new dependencies.

title: fix(workbench): fail fast when a session reaches a terminal state
description:
## Summary

I saw this when testing an internal daily Workbench site, both that it was slow and that the error message was just not understandable when there were issues here.

Running `vip verify --headless-auth --idp okta --workbench-url ...` against Workbench 2026.06 produced 10 failures, all surfaced as the opaque `AssertionError: Locator expected to be visible` after a **90s wait per test**.

The Playwright accessibility snapshot in each traceback showed every launched session sitting at status **`Failed`** with an *"Abnormal exits"* banner — the deployment genuinely could not launch sessions. `vip verify` was correctly catching a real problem, but reporting it slowly and unhelpfully.

## Changes

- **`wait_for_session_active()`** (new helper in `workbench/conftest.py`) polls for `Active` and **fails fast** with an actionable message the moment a terminal state (`Failed`) appears, instead of waiting out `TIMEOUT_SESSION_START`.
- Route all six session-active wait sites through the helper: `test_ide_extensions`, `test_ide_launch`, `test_packages`, `test_data_sources`, `test_sessions`, `test_session_capacity`.
- **`Homepage.session_row_status`** now matches the status whether it is the legacy `div[aria-label]` or the Workbench 2026.06 `button` (text- or aria-label-named), so `Active`/`Suspended`/`Failed` detection survives the UI change.
- Add selftests for the status selector and the failure-message builder.

## Scope / non-goals

- This does **not** fix the underlying deployment problem (sessions failing to launch) — that is environmental and separate. It makes VIP report it quickly and clearly.
- This is **not** issue #280 (extensions *search-input* locator); that did not run in this configuration and remains open.

## Demo

# Fix: fail fast when a Workbench session cannot launch

## Problem

Running `vip verify --headless-auth --idp okta --workbench-url ...` against Workbench 2026.06 produced 10 failures, all reported as the opaque `AssertionError: Locator expected to be visible` after a 90s wait per test.

Investigation (the Playwright accessibility snapshot in each traceback) showed every launched session had status **Failed** with an *'Abnormal exits'* banner — the deployment genuinely could not launch sessions. The test was correctly detecting a real problem, but:

title: fix(connect): reliably clean up VIP content on test failure
description:
Applies the orphaned-resource cleanup pattern from #277 (PR #312, Workbench) to **Connect**, after auditing all three products. Package Manager needs no change — its tests are entirely read-only.

## Problem

Connect deploy tests create content items on the server, but cleanup was a Gherkin `@then` step (`test_content_deploy.py`, `test_packages.py`). In pytest-bdd, a failure in any earlier step stops the scenario, so the cleanup step **never runs on failure** — leaving orphaned content with no backstop. `connect/conftest.py` had no autouse/finalizer cleanup, and the tag-based `cleanup_vip_content()` sweep was only reachable via the manual `vip cleanup` CLI.

## Approach

Cleanup logic is centralized and hardened in `ConnectClient`:

- `_delete_content_verified()` — DELETE (treat **404 as already-gone = success**), then GET to confirm it's gone, with retry. Never raises.
- `cleanup_content(guids)` — deletes a list of GUIDs via the verified path, skipping falsy entries; returns the count confirmed deleted.
- `cleanup_vip_content()` reworked to route through `cleanup_content` (verify + retry) instead of its old silent single-shot loop.
- The existing raising `delete_content` is unchanged (the happy-path step and 409-retry still rely on it).

Test wiring (`src/vip_tests/connect/conftest.py`):

- `_connect_created_guids` — a session-scoped, append-only record of content created this run, **independent of the `_vip_test` tag** (so a tagging hiccup no longer hides an orphan).
- `_connect_content_cleanup` — function-scoped autouse finalizer that deletes exactly this test's content (`[start:]` slice) on **pass or fail**.
- `_connect_end_of_run_sweep` — session-scoped autouse backstop that deletes tracked GUIDs, then runs the tag-based `cleanup_vip_content()` to also catch orphans from prior crashed runs.

The two create steps now append the new content GUID to the tracker immediately after creation (before the failure-prone deploy steps). Under xdist, Connect tests share one worker (`xdist_group("connect")`), so the `[start:]` slice is always this test's content.

7 new selftests (`selftests/test_connect_cleanup.py`) cover the helpers via `httpx.MockTransport`: delete+verify, 404 idempotency, retry-until-gone, falsy-GUID skipping, error paths, and the hardened tag sweep.

## Out of scope

No `vip cleanup` CLI changes (it calls `cleanup_vip_content`, hardened here). No Package Manager changes — audited, read-only, no orphan risk.

## Demo

# Fix: reliable Connect content cleanup

Connect deploy tests previously left content on the server when a test failed before its cleanup step (the cleanup was a Gherkin `@then` step, skipped on failure, with no backstop). Cleanup now lives in `ConnectClient.cleanup_content()` — an idempotent verified delete (404=gone) with retry, always attempting at least one delete. Created content GUIDs are tracked in a session-scoped list and deleted by an autouse per-test finalizer that runs on pass or fail, plus a session-scoped end-of-run sweep that also runs the tag-based cross-run `cleanup_vip_content()`. Package Manager was audited and needs no fix (its tests are read-only).

title: docs: plan for #305 — workbench idle session auto-suspend behavior
description:
## Plan for issue #305: workbench idle session auto-suspend behavior

This PR revises the generated plan with two critical design fixes applied on top of the #349/#336 merges.

### What the plan proposes

- New `[workbench] idle_timeout_minutes` and `idle_grace_seconds` TOML fields in `WorkbenchConfig` (alongside `job_timeout` and `test_packages`, not after `kubernetes`)
- Two new scenarios in `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_session_idle.feature` tagged `@workbench @performance`:
  - **Idle session auto-suspends after the configured timeout** — waits for Suspended state with a configurable grace window (`idle_grace_seconds`, default 60 s)
  - **Active session is not suspended while work is running** — drives the session with periodic activity, then asserts still Active

### Design: periodic activity loop (not a blocking Sys.sleep)

The active-session scenario keeps the session alive by sending **periodic interactive input events** via `rstudio_eval` every 90 seconds across the idle-timeout window — not a single blocking `Sys.sleep` spanning the whole window. A console blocked in `Sys.sleep` is R being *busy*, not a session registering user *activity*; Workbench's idle timeout is driven by interactive input events. The loop:

```python
POLL_INTERVAL_S = 90
end_time = time.monotonic() + (idle_timeout_minutes * 60) + idle_grace_seconds
while time.monotonic() < end_time:
    rstudio_eval(page, "invisible(NULL)", timeout=15_000)
    remaining = end_time - time.monotonic()
    if remaining > 0:
        time.sleep(min(POLL_INTERVAL_S, remaining))
```

Each `rstudio_eval` call types a trivial expression into the RStudio console, emitting a real input event that resets the idle clock — faithful to "activity correctly resets the idle clock" from the issue.

### Configurable grace window

The grace window added on top of `idle_timeout_minutes` is exposed as `idle_grace_seconds: int = 60` in `WorkbenchConfig`. Deployments with high clock drift or slow suspend response can increase this value in `vip.toml`. The `vip.toml.example` documents both fields:

```toml
idle_timeout_minutes = 5   # must be ≤ 15 for the idle scenarios to run
idle_grace_seconds = 60    # seconds added on top of idle_timeout_minutes before asserting suspend
```

### Runtime ceiling: 15 minutes

These scenarios are **only viable against deployments configured with a short idle timeout.** The implementation skips (with a clear message) when `idle_timeout_minutes > 15`:

```python
MAX_VIABLE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES = 15

if timeout > MAX_VIABLE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES:
    pytest.skip(
        f"idle_timeout_minutes={timeout} exceeds the test ceiling of "
        f"{MAX_VIABLE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES} min — configure the deployment "
        "with a shorter timeout to run these scenarios"
    )
```

The `vip.toml.example` will use `idle_timeout_minutes = 5` (not 120) and note the ceiling. A 120-minute example value would imply a 2+ hour test run, which is not viable.

### Note on TERMINAL_SESSION_FAILURE_STATES

`TERMINAL_SESSION_FAILURE_STATES` in `src/vip_tests/workbench/conftest.py:39` contains only `("Failed",)` — `"Suspended"` is intentionally absent, so PR #320's fail-fast logic will not false-fail the idle scenario when the session legitimately reaches Suspended state.

---

title: fix(workbench): reliably clean up VIP sessions on test failure
description:
Closes #277.

## Problem

When a Workbench test failed mid-execution (e.g. during IDE interaction), the session it launched was not reliably terminated, leaving orphaned sessions on the Workbench homepage that users had to quit by hand. The old per-test cleanup quit **all** of the user's sessions, fired a single request without verifying it worked, swallowed every error, and had no end-of-run backstop.

## Approach

Cleanup logic is centralized in `WorkbenchClient.quit_vip_sessions()`:

- Targets **only VIP-named sessions** (`VIP ` and `_vip_` label prefixes), so a real user's sessions are never touched.
- **Verify-and-retry**: after issuing DELETE (falling back to suspend), it re-lists and repeats while VIP sessions remain.
- **Resilient**: never raises on malformed API payloads (non-JSON bodies, non-list responses, `null`/non-string labels); returns the count of *distinct* sessions quit.
- Authenticates with the browser's session cookies, so **no API key is required**.

Test-suite wiring (`src/vip_tests/workbench/conftest.py`):

- The per-test autouse `_cleanup_sessions` fixture now targets only VIP sessions and stashes the latest good cookies.
- A new session-scoped `_wb_cleanup_state` fixture runs a final **end-of-run sweep** as a safety net for sessions orphaned when a per-test cleanup fails outright, with an **API-key fallback** for long runs where browser cookies may have expired.
- The capacity test's duplicated inline httpx cleanup now routes through the same shared helper (TLS config threaded through for self-signed / custom-CA deployments).

15 new selftests cover the predicate and `quit_vip_sessions` (target filtering, retry-until-gone, suspend fallback, malformed payloads, unique counting, error paths) using `httpx.MockTransport`.

## Design note

Cleanup deliberately quits **all** VIP-named sessions rather than scoping to a single scenario's launched names — that broad sweep is what catches orphans whose names weren't tracked. Within a run, Workbench tests are serialized onto one xdist worker, so there's no concurrent sibling session to disturb. The accepted trade-off is that two simultaneous runs sharing one Workbench account could interfere; this is still strictly safer than the prior behavior, which quit *all* sessions regardless of name.

## Demo

# Fix: reliable Workbench session cleanup (#277)

Issue #277: when a Workbench test failed mid-IDE, the session it launched was left running on the homepage, forcing users to quit orphans by hand. Cleanup is now centralized in `WorkbenchClient.quit_vip_sessions()`, which lists sessions and force-quits only VIP-named ones (the `VIP ` and `_vip_` prefixes), then re-lists to verify they are gone and retries. It is resilient to malformed API payloads (non-JSON bodies, null/non-string labels) and counts unique sessions. A session-scoped end-of-run sweep is a safety net so a single failed per-test cleanup no longer orphans a session, with an API-key fallback for long runs where browser cookies may have expired. Cleanup authenticates with the browser's cookies, so no API key is required.

title: fix(workflows): force re-triage cleanup + pin agent models
description:
## Summary

Two workflow refinements, applied together because both surfaced in the
same triage run after #294 / #295 unblocked the App auth path:

### 1. Force unconditional `re-triage` label removal

Step 1a in `issue-triage.md` still framed the label cleanup as a
conditional ("If `re-triage` is among them, run..."). Copilot
consistently skipped this on real runs — it treats conditionals at the
top of a long prompt as optional even with `MUST` framing. Confirmed
again after the live #283 triage cycle: bot opened the plan PR but
left `re-triage` in place.

Rewrite the instruction so there's no decision left:

- Drop the "if present" condition.
- Use `|| true` so the call is fire-and-forget when the label is
  absent.
- Append a short consequence paragraph explaining why skipping breaks
  the maintainer signaling loop.

### 2. Pin agent models per workflow

The default `claude-sonnet-4.5` is now superseded by newer models that
better match the work each workflow does:

- **`issue-triage`** → `claude-opus-4.7`. The enhancement path is the
  demanding one (writing a plan from a freeform issue) and benefits
  from the strongest model. Bug-path runs under triage are rare and
  Opus handles them well too.
- **`implement-plan`** → `claude-sonnet-4.6`. Pure implementation
  work: take a plan, write the code+tests it specifies. Sonnet is the
  right balance of capability and cost here.
- **`preview-screenshot-gallery`** → unchanged. Default is fine; this
  workflow doesn't fit either bug-fix or planning, and runs on every
  PR website preview so it should stay cheap.

The change is set in each workflow's frontmatter:

```yaml
engine:
  id: copilot
  model: <model-name>
```

Regenerated lock files via `gh aw compile --approve`. Confirmed via
`grep COPILOT_MODEL *.lock.yml` that the models are now hard-coded
rather than reading from the `GH_AW_MODEL_AGENT_COPILOT` repo variable.

## Stacked on #295

This PR is built on top of `narrow-workflow-permissions` (#295). Until
#295 lands, this PR's diff will include #295's changes too. Merge #295
first; the diff here will then narrow to just the changes described
above.

## Test plan

- [ ] After this lands (and #295), re-trigger triage on a labeled
      issue and confirm:
  - The `re-triage` label is gone after the workflow run finishes.
  - Workflow logs show `claude-opus-4.7` in `COPILOT_MODEL`.
- [ ] On the next plan PR merge, confirm `implement-plan` runs with
      `claude-sonnet-4.6`.

title: docs: plan for #298 — custom test extension scaffolding
description:
## Plan for issue #298: custom test extension example

This PR revises the plan for adding a `vip scaffold` subcommand and `examples/cross_product_validation/` reference implementation, incorporating primitives now available on `main` after PR #349 and PR #336 merged.

### What the plan proposes

1. **`vip scaffold` subcommand** (`src/vip/cli.py`) — copies the example directory to a user-specified output path; zero copy-paste for the end user
2. **`examples/cross_product_validation/`** — a ready-to-run extension example with:
   - Connect runtime version checks (`connect_client.r_versions()` / `.python_versions()`)
   - **DESeq2 (R) and PyDeSEQ2 (Python) package install verification** on Connect, following the deploy-bundle pattern from `src/vip_tests/connect/test_packages.py`
   - **Workbench package install verification** via `terminal_run` from `src/vip_tests/workbench/exec.py` (merged in #349)
   - Skippable package-install scenarios via a `check_packages` fixture flag
3. **Selftest coverage** (`selftests/test_cli_scaffold.py`) asserting on scaffolded content, not just file existence

### Relationship to #303 / PR #327

PR #327 (in-flight) adds built-in Workbench session-dialog version checks using `R_VERSION_DROPDOWN` / `PYTHON_VERSION_DROPDOWN` selectors. This example intentionally does not duplicate those scenarios. The README will point readers to `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_runtime_versions.py` for that coverage; the example focuses on the extension-author pattern and package install verification that #303 does not cover.

### Key design decisions

- Example name: `examples/cross_product_validation/` (generic, not GxP-specific)
- Scaffold: simple file copy; no interactive templating (users hand-edit `conftest.py`)
- No fixture name collision: the example reuses `expected_r_versions` / `expected_python_versions` from the installed plugin rather than redefining them
- Auto-skip markers: `@pytest.mark.connect` / `@pytest.mark.workbench` on every `@scenario` function (not just feature-level Gherkin tags)

See `thoughts/shared/plans/2026-05-29-issue-298-custom-test-scaffolding.md` for the full plan.

title: feat(cli): support help flag before the subcommand
description:
## Summary

A small thing I came across that confused me when using vip today- while "vip verify -h" gave me the info I wanted, I first tried "vip -h verify" and that gave me the top-level info which was confusing.

`vip -h verify` previously printed the top-level help instead of the `verify` subcommand's help, because argparse's top-level parser consumes `-h`/`--help` before delegating to a subparser. The only working form was `vip verify -h`.

This adds a small preprocessing helper, `_reorder_help_args`, that runs before `parse_args()`. When a help flag appears *ahead* of a recognized subcommand, it moves the flag to the end of the arg list so the subparser handles it and prints its own help. It reuses the existing `subcommand_parsers` dict for the command names, so it stays in sync automatically.

## Behavior

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `vip -h verify` | now shows full verify help (incl. `--headless-auth`) |
| `vip verify -h` | unchanged, still works |
| `vip -h auth mint-connect-key` | shows the nested subcommand help |
| `vip -h` (no subcommand) | still shows top-level help |

Arg lists are left untouched when there's no help flag, when help already follows the command, or when there's no subcommand.

## Testing

- New `selftests/test_cli_verify.py::TestReorderHelpArgs` (6 cases) — all pass
- Full selftest suite: 570 passed, 3 skipped
- ruff lint + format (0.15.0): clean

title: ci: narrow agentic workflow permissions to match the App's grants
description:
## Summary

The first live run of the triage workflow after #294 failed at the
`actions/create-github-app-token` step with:

> HTTP 422: The permissions requested are not granted to this installation.

The default `permissions: read-all` was being expanded by gh-aw into a
request for read access to a long list of scopes (`actions`, `checks`,
`deployments`, `discussions`, `packages`, `pages`, `security-events`,
`statuses`, `vulnerability-alerts`, etc.) that the App is not granted.
GitHub refuses the mint outright when *any* requested permission is
absent from the installation.

The App has exactly: `contents`, `issues`, `pull-requests` (read+write),
and `metadata` (read). So the workflows have been narrowed to match.

## What changes

All three gh-aw workflow `.md` files:

- **Replace `permissions: read-all`** with an explicit read-only block:
  ```yaml
  permissions:
    contents: read
    issues: read
    pull-requests: read
  ```
  Writes happen exclusively through safe-outputs (gh-aw strict mode
  blocks workflow-level `*: write` anyway). The safe-outputs job mints
  its own token with `contents: write` / `issues: write` /
  `pull-requests: write` for the duration of the operation.

- **Add `discussions: false`** to each `add-comment` safe-output. By
  default gh-aw requests `discussions: write` because `add-comment`
  *could* target a discussion thread; ours don't. The flag drops that
  unneeded permission so the safe-outputs token mint only requests
  what the App grants.

Regenerated the three `.lock.yml` files via `gh aw compile --approve`.
Confirmed via `grep "permission-" *.lock.yml` that the minted tokens
now request exactly `contents`, `issues`, `pull-requests` (in matching
read/write pairs) and nothing else.

## Test plan

- [ ] After merge, re-trigger the triage workflow on #288 (or another
      open issue) and confirm:
  - `Generate GitHub App token` step succeeds (no HTTP 422).
  - Workflow runs to completion.
  - Bot still opens a real PR.
- [ ] Spot-check the next implement-plan and preview-screenshot-gallery
      runs to ensure they also mint tokens successfully.

title: chore: authenticate agentic workflows via GitHub App
description:
## Summary

Configures the three gh-aw workflows (issue-triage, implement-plan,
preview-screenshot-gallery) to authenticate using a dedicated GitHub
App instead of the default GITHUB_TOKEN. Unblocks the bot's PR-creation
path that was previously falling back to opening notification issues
(as on #291).

### Why

GITHUB_TOKEN cannot create pull requests when the repo's "Allow GitHub
Actions to create and approve pull requests" setting is off. Rather
than flip that setting globally (which would expand the attack surface
for every workflow), we mint a short-lived installation token from a
purpose-built App scoped to this repo and granted only the permissions
these workflows need.

### What changes

- Added `github-app:` blocks under both `tools.github` and
  `safe-outputs:` in all three workflow `.md` source files.
- Regenerated all three `.lock.yml` files via `gh aw compile --approve`.
  The compiled lock files inject `actions/create-github-app-token@v3.2.0`
  setup steps that mint the installation token.

### Security review

gh-aw's safe-update mode flagged this compile because two new restricted
secrets are now referenced from the lock files. Reviewed both:

- `POSIT_VIP_TRIAGE_CLIENT_ID` — GitHub App Client ID. Public identifier,
  not a credential on its own. Provisioned by CloudOps.
- `POSIT_VIP_TRIAGE_PEM` — App private key (PEM-encoded). Provisioned by
  CloudOps. Only referenced as input to `actions/create-github-app-token`,
  which exchanges it for a short-lived installation token. Never logged,
  never written to artifacts.

New action introduced: `actions/create-github-app-token@v3.2.0`
(commit-pinned to `bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1`). Official
GitHub action used to mint App tokens.

No network-allowlist changes from this compile.

### Behavioral impact

- Bot-authored PRs and comments will be attributed to the App identity
  instead of `github-actions[bot]`.
- Once this merges, re-triggering the triage workflow on #288 should
  produce a real PR rather than a fallback notification issue.

## Test plan

- [ ] After merge, re-trigger the triage workflow on #288 via an
      `@Copilot retry` comment from a CODEOWNER and confirm:
  - The workflow completes without permission errors.
  - A real PR is opened (not a notification issue like #291).
  - PR author is the new App, not `github-actions[bot]`.
- [ ] Close #291 referencing the new PR once the above succeeds.
- [ ] Spot-check next implement-plan and preview-screenshot-gallery
      runs still function normally.

### Follow-up additions (commit 2)

Brought over the two pieces from the superseded #287 that aren't
inherently auth-related:

- **`draft: false`** on `safe-outputs.create-pull-request` in
  `issue-triage.md` and `implement-plan.md`. gh-aw's default forces
  bot PRs to draft state; this overrides so they enter CI/review
  immediately on creation. (`preview-screenshot-gallery` has no
  `create-pull-request` block, so no change there.)
- **`.github/triage-bot/README.md`** rewrite: replaces the old
  "Required secrets" section with one covering the new
  `POSIT_VIP_TRIAGE_CLIENT_ID` / `POSIT_VIP_TRIAGE_PEM` secrets,
  required App permissions, and what fails if credentials are
  missing.

Supersedes #287.

title: fix(issue-triage): promote pre-run cleanup to dedicated Step 1a
description:
## Summary

Restructures the issue-triage workflow's Step 1 so the `re-triage`
removal and idempotent label-bootstrap commands live in their own
numbered, MUST-framed `Step 1a — pre-run cleanup` block instead of
sitting as loose paragraphs at the tail of the gate logic.

### Why

In #288's first re-run, the bot reached Step 4 (enhancement path) and
wrote the plan file successfully, but never executed the
`gh issue edit --remove-label re-triage` instruction that was buried in
Step 1's narrative. Same story for the `gh label create` bootstrap:
only the two labels the bot ended up *applying* (`triaged-by-bot`,
`needs-human-triage`) got created — `re-triage` and `skip-triage` had to
be created by hand for the re-triage flow to work at all.

The pattern is consistent: Copilot tends to skip "incidental" guidance
that isn't called out as imperative steps, especially when a later
section (Step 4 here) is framed as the deliverable. Promoting the
cleanup to its own numbered step with explicit `MUST` wording removes
the ambiguity.

### What changes

- New `Step 1a — pre-run cleanup` section with two numbered actions.
- Same shell commands as before, no behavior intent change.
- Added a best-effort failure clause so a transient label-API hiccup
  can't derail the run into Step 5.

### What does not change

- Step 1's gate conditions are untouched.
- The bash allowlist is untouched (`gh issue edit *` and `gh label
  create *` already permit the calls).
- Steps 2–6 are byte-identical.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verifiable only on the next live triage cycle. When an issue
      goes through a re-triage (or a fresh enhancement-path run lands),
      confirm the `re-triage` label is gone after the workflow run
      finishes, and that the four triage labels all exist.
- [ ] Tracked separately: CloudOps work to enable
      "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" so the
      enhancement path can actually open a PR end-to-end (currently
      falls back to opening a notification issue, as on #291).

description:
## Summary

Adds structured GitHub issue forms so new issues land with consistent
information and the labels that the triage agent already keys on.

- `bug_report.yml` — labels `bug`, required fields for VIP version, affected

title: fix(triage): bypass org PR-create block + honor non-draft preference
description:
## Summary

Adds `github-token` and `draft: false` to `safe-outputs.create-pull-request` in both `issue-triage.md` and `implement-plan.md`:

- `github-token: ${{ secrets.TRIAGE_BOT_TOKEN }}` — bypasses the `posit-dev` org policy that blocks `GITHUB_TOKEN` from creating PRs. Observed in the live run on #283 (gh-aw fell back to review-issue #286).
- `draft: false` — overrides gh-aw's default, which forced bot PRs to draft despite the agent requesting otherwise.

Updates `.github/triage-bot/README.md` with setup instructions for the new `TRIAGE_BOT_TOKEN` secret, covering both the GitHub App (recommended) and fine-grained PAT options.

## Security review note

The only new secret introduced is `TRIAGE_BOT_TOKEN`. It is consumed exclusively by gh-aw's `safe-outputs.create-pull-request` handler (visible in the compiled `.lock.yml`); it is not exposed to agent-controlled bash commands. Compiled with `gh aw compile --approve` after reviewing the diff.

## Behavior without the secret

If `TRIAGE_BOT_TOKEN` is unset, the workflow continues to function via the review-issue fallback — same behavior as before this PR. The setting is additive.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (`ci.yml`, `pr-title.yml`)
- [ ] After landing, set `TRIAGE_BOT_TOKEN` (either an App installation token or a fine-grained PAT)
- [ ] Apply `re-triage` to issue #283 and verify the bot now opens the PR directly (non-draft) instead of falling back to a review issue

title: feat: add agentic issue triage workflows
description:
## Summary

- Adds two gh-aw agents under `.github/workflows/`:
  - `issue-triage.md` — runs on every newly opened issue; classifies bug vs enhancement; opens a PR (bug, high confidence) or a plan PR (enhancement) or posts a `needs-human-triage` comment.
  - `implement-plan.md` — fires when a plan PR merges to `main`; opens the corresponding implementation PR.
- Engine: `copilot`. Reuses existing gh-aw secrets — no new provisioning required.
- Scope guards: path denylist (release/CI/config files) + new-file whitelist (`selftests/`, `src/vip_tests/`, `thoughts/shared/plans/`, `validation_docs/`).
- Labels: opt-out via `skip-triage`, re-run via `re-triage`, bookkeeping via `triaged-by-bot` / `needs-human-triage`.
- Docs added at `docs/agentic-workflows.md` and `.github/triage-bot/README.md`.

## Also includes

- Migrates `preview-screenshot-gallery.md` from deprecated playwright MCP mode to CLI mode (separate commit).
- Bumps the gh-aw compiler from v0.67.1 → v0.74.8 as a side effect, regenerating `preview-screenshot-gallery.lock.yml`, `.github/aw/actions-lock.json`, and `.github/dependabot.yml`.

## Test plan

- [x] CI passes (`ci.yml`, `pr-title.yml`)
- [ ] Open a synthetic bug issue with clear repro → bot opens a fix PR with a selftest and showboat demo
- [ ] Open a synthetic enhancement issue → bot opens a plan PR; comment summary on the original issue
- [ ] Merge the plan PR → `implement-plan` opens an implementation PR
- [ ] Open an issue with empty body → bot posts `needs-human-triage` comment, no PR opened
- [ ] Apply `skip-triage` to a fresh issue → no bot action
- [ ] Apply `re-triage` to a `triaged-by-bot` issue → bot runs again and removes `re-triage`
- [ ] preview-screenshot-gallery workflow still runs on the next preview deploy and posts inline screenshots (CLI-mode migration)

title: fix(auth): surface workbench auth failures and scope cache per URL
description:
## Summary

As I was trying two internal testing sites with okta, I came across some issues with auth that I've fixed up here.

- **Workbench skip messages now name the cause.** When `--interactive-auth` / `--headless-auth` could not establish a Workbench session, browser tests skipped with a hard-coded "Interactive auth storage state did not authenticate Workbench" line regardless of which mode was active. `_authenticate_workbench` now returns the failure reason (PlaywrightError, 2-minute timeout, or last URL on the login page) and the workbench login fixture quotes it in the skip text along with the active mode's CLI flag and a short list of next steps.
- **Auth cache invalidates on URL mismatch.** `.vip-auth-cache.json` is one slot per checkout directory, so a second run targeting a different connect-url or workbench-url silently reused the first run's storage state and API key. The cache now records both URLs and refuses to load when either differs from the request. URL normalization lowercases only scheme + netloc (paths are case-sensitive per RFC 3986) and strips at most one trailing slash so `/app/` and `/app//` remain distinct.
- **`workbench_auth_error` propagates across xdist workers** via `pytest_configure_node` / `_restore_worker_auth` so the new skip message is consistent under `-n auto`.

## Test plan

- [x] `just check` (ruff lint + format)
- [x] `uv run pytest selftests/ -q` (559 passing, 3 expected skips)
- [x] Reproduce the original skip on a real OIDC deployment with mismatched Connect/Workbench sessions and verify the new skip message names the right flag and quotes the captured reason
- [x] Verify cache invalidation: run `vip verify` against site A, then site B from the same directory within 4 hours, and confirm site B re-authenticates instead of reusing site A's state

v0.72.1

🌟 Release Highlights

v0.72.1 delivers a new developer-facing lint command, critical compiler correctness fixes, and improved shared workflow ergonomics — all driven largely by community-reported issues.

✨ What's New

  • gh aw lint — fast lock-file validation (#30704): New gh aw lint command runs actionlint directly against existing .lock.yml files — no recompile, no extra scanners. Perfect for a lightweight CI gate to catch syntax errors before pushing. Supports --dir, explicit file paths, and optional --shellcheck/--pyflakes checks.

  • Import engine.mcp.tool-timeout from shared workflows (#30634): Shared workflows wrapping slow MCP servers (e.g. Repo Mind Light) can now declare engine.mcp.tool-timeout and engine.mcp.session-timeout once, and consumers inherit those values automatically — no more duplicating timeout configs in every consumer. Consumer-declared values still take precedence.

  • First-party coding-agent skill for gh aw (#27259): Added a router skill that gives coding agents (Copilot, Claude, etc.) structured guidance on creating, debugging, and updating agentic workflows using the gh aw CLI.

  • Shared skip-if-match dedup component: The common "open issue/PR by title prefix" deduplication query is now a shared compiler-imported component, eliminating copy-paste duplication across dozens of workflows.

🐛 Bug Fixes & Improvements

  • && preserved in compiled workflow expressions (#30695): Go's HTML escaping was converting && to \u0026\u0026 inside AWF config JSON embedded in .lock.yml files, corrupting ${{ ... && ... }} expressions and causing workflow parse failures. Fixed by switching to json.Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false).

  • safe-outputs permission regression fixed (#30733): When update-project appeared alongside add-comment/add-labels, the minted App token was incorrectly downgraded to issues:read instead of issues:write, silently failing issue mutations.

  • Conclusion comment now reflects safe_outputs failures (#30662): The conclusion job was reporting ✅ success even when safe_outputs failed (e.g., 422 on PR review submission). The job now correctly propagates safe_outputs status.

  • Firewall binary version corrected (#30705, #30191): v0.71.1 was referencing a non-existent gh-aw-firewall version, causing 404s on AWF binary install. This release ships with the correct firewall v0.25.29 (which also includes the healthcheck fix).

  • Playwright mode: cli recognized by compiler (#30088): gh aw compile now correctly accepts mode: cli in Playwright tool configuration.

  • COPILOT_API_KEY dummy key no longer triggers over-billing (#30324): The dummy byok-key placeholder introduced in v0.71 was causing 10–100x premium request over-billing compared to v0.68. Fixed.

Mypy Release Notes

Next Release

Mypy 2.1

We’ve just uploaded mypy 2.1.0 to the Python Package Index (PyPI). Mypy is a static type checker for Python. This release includes new features, performance improvements and bug fixes. You can install it as follows:

python3 -m pip install -U mypy

You can read the full documentation for this release on Read the Docs.

librt.vecs: Fast Growable Array Type for Mypyc

The new librt.vecs module provides an efficient growable array type vec that is optimized for mypyc use. It provides fast, packed arrays with integer and floating point value types, which can be several times faster than list, and tens of times faster than array.array in code compiled using mypyc. It also supports nested vec objects and non-value-type items, such as vec[vec[str]].

Refer to the documentation for the details.

Contributed by Jukka Lehtosalo.

librt.random: Fast Pseudo-Random Number Generation

The new librt.random module provides fast pseudo-random number generation that is optimized for code compiled using mypyc. It can be 3x to 10x faster than the stdlib random module in compiled code.

Refer to the documentation for the details.

title: feat: add VIP_TEST_TOTP_SECRET for unattended --headless-auth MFA
description:
## Summary

Add in 'VIP_TEST_TOTP_SECRET' to be used with service accounts only to allow for more automated runs of VIP.  This also removes some plans files checked in accidentally previously.

- New `vip.totp` module (`validate_secret`, `get_code`, `ENV_VAR`) generates the current 6-digit TOTP code from a base32 seed in `VIP_TEST_TOTP_SECRET`, falling back to the existing interactive `input()` prompt when the env var is unset or whitespace-only.
- `start_headless_auth` validates the seed before launching Playwright (fail-fast with a clear error). The Keycloak and Okta IdP TOTP fill sites in `src/vip/idp.py` now call `totp.get_code(...)` instead of `input(...).strip()`. The Okta push-MFA fallback is intentionally unchanged.
- Docs surface the feature in `--headless-auth --help`, `vip.toml.example`, `AGENTS.md`, and the getting-started website page, with a consistent **"equivalent to bypassing 2FA — use only with dedicated test service accounts"** warning.
- Adds `pyotp ~= 2.9` (zero transitive deps, MIT licensed).

**Security:** the seed and the generated code are never logged, never appear in error messages, and never reach the JSON report or HTML report. Only the env var *name* is surfaced for operator troubleshooting.

**Out of scope (separate spec when needed):** K8s job mode (`--k8s`), non-TOTP factors (push, SMS, security key), host-clock-skew handling.

## Test plan
- [x] `selftests/test_totp.py` (7 tests): valid / invalid / empty seed; env-set generates pyotp-matching code; env-set bypasses `input()`; env-unset prompts; whitespace-only env falls through to prompt.
- [x] `selftests/test_auth.py::TestStartHeadlessAuthValidation` (+2 tests): invalid seed raises `AuthConfigError` BEFORE Playwright launches; valid seed does not surface a seed-related error.
- [x] `selftests/test_idp.py` (+2 tests): Keycloak runtime test asserts `totp.get_code` is called (and `input()` is patched to raise); Okta source-inspection asserts no raw verification-code `input()` remains.
- [x] Full selftest suite: 512 passed, 3 skipped.
- [x] `just check` clean (ruff lint + format).
- [x] `validation_docs/demo-totp-seed.md` — verified by `showboat verify`.
- [x] Manual end-to-end against an MFA-enabled IdP cannot run in CI (same constraint as all other product tests in VIP).

## Demo
See `validation_docs/demo-totp-seed.md` for showboat output.

title: fix(auth): make headless-auth mint work on sub-path Connect URLs
description:
## Summary

As I was working on using an internal Connect site with this, I used the "/connect" path as part of the URL, which brought back confusing error messages and didn't work as the API creation failed.  Fix both the error messages and handle things properly when the "/connect" path is added on to the URL given"

- Fixes a misleading mint failure when `--headless-auth` / `--interactive-auth` runs against a Connect deployment whose dashboard sits on a sub-path (e.g. `https://host/connect/`) while the API stays at the host root.
- Probes `/__api__/server_settings` to auto-correct the configured URL on a positive `dashboard_path` match, propagates the corrected URL through xdist workers, and sends the create-API-key POST body as JSON (Connect 2026.05 returns HTTP 400 for form-encoded).
- Replaces an opaque "API key minting failed" with concrete diagnostics (cookie jar contents, XSRF preview, `/server_settings` probe, likely-misconfigured-URL pointer).

## What changed
- `_resolve_connect_api_base()` in `src/vip/auth.py` probes the configured URL first, then the host root, and switches only when the root API's advertised `dashboard_path` matches the configured sub-path. Bails cleanly on transport errors, non-JSON 200s, and ambiguous payloads.
- Both `start_headless_auth` and `start_interactive_auth` call the resolver before mint; the corrected URL flows onto `InteractiveAuthSession._connect_url`.
- `pytest_configure` and `_restore_worker_auth` in `src/vip/plugin.py` sync `vip_cfg.connect.url` from the session so xdist workers build their `ConnectClient` against the same base mint succeeded at.
- `_create_api_key_via_session` sends `json={"name": ...}` instead of `data={"name": ...}` — matches every other Connect POST in the codebase.
- Mint failure now logs the cookie jar (full + the subset sent to `/__api__/v1/user`), the XSRF header preview, and a `/server_settings` follow-up probe; existing tests for these diagnostics are exercised in `selftests/test_auth.py`.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pytest selftests/` — 521 passed, 3 skipped (5 new tests: 1 missing-`dashboard_path` case + 4 worker-restore cases + the resolver matrix)
- [x] `uv run ruff check src/ src/vip_tests/ selftests/ examples/` and `ruff format --check ...` — clean
- [x] Manual: `uv run vip verify --headless-auth --idp okta --connect-url https://connect.staging.pct.posit.it/connect --verbose` — URL auto-correction prints, mint succeeds, content tests start running
- [ ] Manual: `vip verify` against a Connect deployment without a sub-path — confirm the resolver leaves the URL unchanged (`primary_resp.status_code == 200` short-circuit)

title: fix(install): detect stale chromium cache via pinned revision
description:
## Summary

I was noticing that tests couldn't be run even after I ran "vip install", as it complain about my Playwright version.  This fixes things so an old  Playwright install is detected and an upgrade happens

- `chromium_installed()` previously matched any `chromium-*` directory, so a stale build from an older Playwright pin made `vip install` say "nothing to install" — and Playwright then failed at launch with its own "please run playwright install" message, undermining the whole point of `vip install`.
- Now we read the expected revision from `playwright/driver/package/browsers.json` shipped inside the installed Playwright package and look for the specific `chromium-<revision>` directory.
- Falls back to the old loose match when the revision cannot be determined so a broken Playwright install does not block `vip install`.
- New selftests cover the bug repro, the matching-revision case, the default lookup, the fallback, and a live read of `browsers.json`.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest selftests/install/test_playwright.py -v` (new and existing playwright selftests)
- [x] `uv run pytest selftests/ -q` (full selftest suite: 505 passed, 3 skipped)
- [x] `just check` (ruff lint + format)
- [x] `uv run vip install --dry-run` against real cache with stale `chromium-1208` correctly plans to install chromium
- [x] `showboat verify` on `validation_docs/demo-chromium-revision-check.md`

We’ve just uploaded mypy 2.1.0 to the Python Package Index (PyPI). Mypy is a static type checker for Python. This release includes new features, performance improvements and bug fixes. You can install it as follows:

python3 -m pip install -U mypy

You can read the full documentation for this release on Read the Docs.

librt.vecs: Fast Growable Array Type for Mypyc

The new librt.vecs module provides an efficient growable array type vec that is optimized for mypyc use. It provides fast, packed arrays with integer and floating point value types, which can be several times faster than list, and tens of times faster than array.array in code compiled using mypyc. It also supports nested vec objects and non-value-type items, such as vec[vec[str]].

Refer to the documentation for the details.

Contributed by Jukka Lehtosalo.

librt.random: Fast Pseudo-Random Number Generation

The new librt.random module provides fast pseudo-random number generation that is optimized for code compiled using mypyc. It can be 3x to 10x faster than the stdlib random module in compiled code.

Refer to the documentation for the details.

Contributed by Jukka Lehtosalo (PR 21433).
