title: feat(performance): add concurrent user load tests for each product
description:
Issue #117 requested load tests focused on concurrent users (not large sessions). The existing `test_concurrency` scenarios only hit anonymous health-check endpoints — these new tests simulate authenticated users making real API calls simultaneously.

## New: `test_load` scenarios

Three `Scenario Outline` definitions under `src/vip_tests/performance/`, one per product, each running at **10, 20, 50, and 100 concurrent users** (12 test cases total):

| Product | Endpoint | Auth |
|---------|----------|------|
| Connect | `GET /__api__/v1/content` | API key |
| Workbench | `GET /api/server/settings` | API key |
| Package Manager | `GET /__api__/repos` | ****** |

Each scenario asserts:
- Success rate ≥ 95%
- p95 response time ≤ `performance.p95_response_time`

The user count is passed directly from the `Examples` table into each `When` step, so test IDs are clearly labeled (e.g. `test_connect_handles_users_concurrent_authenticated_users[100]`).

Auto-skips per product when not configured, consistent with the rest of the performance suite.

title: fix(example-report): skip Package Manager when RSPM_LICENSE is unavailable
description:
`example-report.yml` hard-fails when `RSPM_LICENSE` is empty (Dependabot/fork PRs without maintainer approval). PM falls back to trial mode, and the trial in `ubuntu2204-2024.08.0` has expired. `packagemanager-smoke.yml` already handles this by checking for the secret and skipping all PM steps gracefully — `example-report.yml` had no such guard.

## Changes

- **`Check for RSPM_LICENSE` step** — sets `pm-license.available` output to `true`/`false`, mirroring the pattern in `packagemanager-smoke.yml`
- **PM steps conditionalized** — `Start Package Manager`, `Wait for PM`, `Provision repos`, `Resolve PM version`, and `Stop Package Manager` all gated on `steps.pm-license.outputs.available == 'true'`
- **`Check for license errors` step** — surfaces expired/invalid license as a workflow annotation with an actionable step summary, matching `packagemanager-smoke.yml`
- **Dynamic `vip.toml`** — `[package_manager]` section and deployment name included only when PM is available

```yaml
- name: Check for RSPM_LICENSE
  id: pm-license
  run: |
    if [ -z "${{ secrets.RSPM_LICENSE }}" ]; then
      echo "RSPM_LICENSE secret not configured — skipping Package Manager steps"
      echo "available=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    else
      echo "available=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    fi

- name: Start Package Manager
  if: steps.pm-license.outputs.available == 'true'
  ...
```

Updates `astral-sh/setup-uv` from 5 to 7
Release notes

Sourced from astral-sh/setup-uv's releases.

v7.2.1 🌈 update known checksums up to 0.9.28

Changes

🧰 Maintenance

  • chore: update known checksums for 0.9.28 @github-actions[bot] (#744)
  • chore: update known checksums for 0.9.27 @github-actions[bot] (#742)
  • chore: update known checksums for 0.9.26 @github-actions[bot] (#734)
  • chore: update known checksums for 0.9.25 @github-actions[bot] (#733)
  • chore: update known checksums for 0.9.24 @github-actions[bot] (#730)

📚 Documentation

  • Clarify impact of using actions/setup-python @​eifinger (#732)

⬆️ Dependency updates

  • Bump zizmorcore/zizmor-action from 0.3.0 to 0.4.1 @dependabot[bot] (#741)

v7.0.0 🌈 node24 and a lot of bugfixes

Changes

This release comes with a load of bug fixes and a speed up. Because of switching from node20 to node24 it is also a breaking change. If you are running on GitHub hosted runners this will just work, if you are using self-hosted runners make sure, that your runners are up to date. If you followed the normal installation instructions your self-hosted runner will keep itself updated.

This release also removes the deprecated input server-url which was used to download uv releases from a different server. The manifest-file input supersedes that functionality by adding a flexible way to define available versions and where they should be downloaded from.

Fixes

  • The action now respects when the environment variable UV_CACHE_DIR is already set and does not overwrite it. It now also finds cache-dir settings in config files if you set them.
  • Some users encountered problems that cache pruning took forever because they had some uv processes running in the background. Starting with uv version 0.8.24 this action uses uv cache prune --ci --force to ignore the running processes
  • If you just want to install uv but not have it available in path, this action now respects UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH
  • Some other actions also set the env var UV_CACHE_DIR. This action can now deal with that but as this could lead to unwanted behavior in some edgecases a warning is now displayed.

Improvements

If you are using minimum version specifiers for the version of uv to install for example

[tool.uv]
required-version = ">=0.8.17"

This action now detects that and directly uses the latest version. Previously it would download all available releases from the uv repo to determine the highest matching candidate for the version specifier, which took much more time.

If you are using other specifiers like 0.8.x this action still needs to download all available releases because the specifier defines an upper bound (not 0.9.0 or later) and "latest" would possibly not satisfy that.

Updates `actions/upload-artifact` from 4 to 7
Release notes

Sourced from actions/upload-artifact's releases.

v7.0.0

v7 What's new

Direct Uploads

Adds support for uploading single files directly (unzipped). Callers can set the new archive parameter to false to skip zipping the file during upload. Right now, we only support single files. The action will fail if the glob passed resolves to multiple files. The name parameter is also ignored with this setting. Instead, the name of the artifact will be the name of the uploaded file.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

Updates `actions/download-artifact` from 4 to 8
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v7...v8.0.0

v7.0.0

v7 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v7 now runs on Node.js 24 (runs.using: node24) and requires a minimum Actions Runner version of 2.327.1. If you are using self-hosted runners, ensure they are updated before upgrading.

Node.js 24

This release updates the runtime to Node.js 24. v6 had preliminary support for Node 24, however this action was by default still running on Node.js 20. Now this action by default will run on Node.js 24.

description:
## Summary

- Renames the package from `vip` to `posit-vip` in `pyproject.toml` to match the existing PyPI project name
- Updates the PyPI environment URL in `publish.yml` to reflect the correct project name

The publish workflow was failing with `403 Forbidden` because the trusted publisher on PyPI is configured for `posit-vip`, but the built artifacts were named `vip`.

The import path, CLI command (`vip`), and pytest plugin entrypoint are unchanged — only the distribution name seen by PyPI changes.

title: docs: four-layer test architecture and add test architect agent
description:
## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive documentation for VIP's four-layer testing architecture and introduces a test architect agent to guide test design and implementation.

## Changes

- **New documentation** (`docs/test-architecture.md`): Complete guide to VIP's four-layer testing architecture with examples for each layer (test scenarios, step definitions, driver ports, and adapters). Includes rationale for the architecture, VIP-specific conventions, and a checklist for adding new tests.

- **New agent** (`.claude/agents/test-architect.md`): Automated test architect agent that helps design and review acceptance tests following the four-layer pattern. Includes role definition, layer-by-layer guidance, review checklist, and anti-pattern detection.

- **Updated AGENTS.md**: Added summary of the four-layer architecture with links to the new documentation and agent, plus key principles for test design.

## Key Principles Documented

- **Layer 1 (Test)**: Pure Gherkin scenarios with product tags, no implementation details
- **Layer 2 (DSL)**: Step definitions using pytest_bdd with fixtures, thin logic
- **Layer 3 (Driver Port)**: Client interfaces in `src/vip/clients/` returning dicts
- **Layer 4 (Driver Adapter)**: httpx for API, Playwright for UI implementations

Each layer protects against different kinds of changes (business rules, API changes, UI redesigns), making tests maintainable and resilient.

Adds support for uploading single files directly (unzipped). Callers can set the new archive parameter to false to skip zipping the file during upload. Right now, we only support single files. Updates `actions/download-artifact` from 4 to 8
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. title: feat(ci): add license error annotations to smoke test workflows
description:
## Background and Motivation

When a product license expires, smoke test jobs fail with a generic "Process completed with exit code 1" buried deep in container logs ([example run](https://github.com/posit-dev/vip/actions/runs/23032486482/job/66893505553?pr=63#step:13:248)). Finding the actual cause requires scrolling through hundreds of lines of Docker output to spot the license warning. This makes it hard to identify expired license keys quickly.

## Design Decisions

- **`::error` annotations over just summaries**: GitHub Actions annotations appear at the top of the workflow run page and in PR checks, making license errors visible without opening the job logs.
- **Step summary for actionable context**: The annotation identifies the error; the step summary tells you which repository secret to update.
- **`if: failure()` guard**: The license check step only runs when a preceding step fails, adding zero overhead to passing runs.
- **Container log grep approach**: All three products write license status to their container logs on startup. Grepping for `expired|invalid|unable|not activated` covers the known error patterns from Connect, Workbench, and Package Manager.

## Changes

All three smoke test workflows (`connect-smoke.yml`, `workbench-smoke.yml`, `packagemanager-smoke.yml`) gain a **"Check for license errors"** step placed after container startup:

- Runs only on failure (`if: failure()`)
- Greps Docker container logs for license-related error messages
- Emits `::error title=License Error::` annotations visible on the workflow run page
- Writes a "License Error" section to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` naming the specific secret to update

Connect uses `docker ps --filter` to find the container (since `with-connect` may not expose a container name on failure). Workbench and Package Manager reference their known container names directly.

Additionally fixes a pre-existing shellcheck SC2129 warning in the Package Manager summary step.

## Testing

- `actionlint` passes clean on all three modified workflow files
- The license check step is guarded by `if: failure()` so it won't affect passing runs
- The grep patterns match the actual error messages observed in the [failing run](https://github.com/posit-dev/vip/actions/runs/23032486482/job/66893505553?pr=63#step:13:248)

title: fix(ci): use matrix version in smoke test artifact names
description:
## Background and Motivation

The scheduled Workbench smoke test run fails with a 409 Conflict when
uploading artifacts:

> Failed to CreateArtifact: an artifact with this name already exists on the workflow run

This happens because artifact names use the **resolved** product version
(e.g. `2026.01.1+403.pro11`), which can be identical across matrix
entries. On scheduled runs the matrix includes both a pinned tag
(`ubuntu2204-2026.01.1`) and a floating tag (`ubuntu2204`), and when
they resolve to the same version the second upload collides with the
first.

## Proposed Changes

Use the matrix input value (the Docker image tag) instead of the
resolved version in artifact names across all three smoke workflows:

- `workbench-smoke.yml` — `matrix.workbench-version`
- `connect-smoke.yml` — `matrix.connect-version`
- `packagemanager-smoke.yml` — `matrix.pm-version`

Matrix values are guaranteed unique per job, so artifact names can
never collide regardless of what version the containers resolve to.

## Testing

- `just check` passes (ruff lint + format)
- `uv run pytest selftests/ -v` — 89 passed
- Validated with `actionlint` — no new issues

title: ci: add status gate jobs to smoke test workflows
description:
Smoke tests are skipped on dependabot PRs (`if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'`), which means required status checks never report — blocking merge.

Adds a `status` gate job to each smoke test workflow that can be used as the required check instead:

- **`Connect Smoke Tests Status`** in `connect-smoke.yml`
- **`Package Manager Smoke Tests Status`** in `packagemanager-smoke.yml`
- **`Workbench Smoke Tests Status`** in `workbench-smoke.yml`

Each gate job uses `if: always()` with `needs:` on the smoke job, passing when upstream succeeded or was skipped, failing on failure or cancellation:

```yaml
status:
  name: Connect Smoke Tests Status
  if: always()
  needs: [connect-smoke]
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Check smoke test result
      run: |
        if [ "${{ needs.connect-smoke.result }}" = "failure" ] || [ "${{ needs.connect-smoke.result }}" = "cancelled" ]; then
          exit 1
        fi
```

After merge, update branch protection required checks to reference the `*Status` job names.

title: fix: use SSH deploy key for semantic-release push
description:
## Summary

- Add `ignore_token_for_push = true` to semantic-release config so it uses the SSH deploy key (set via checkout) instead of constructing an HTTPS URL with `GH_TOKEN`
- Without this, branch protection blocks the push because `GITHUB_TOKEN` HTTPS pushes don't get the deploy key bypass

Updates `actions/upload-artifact` from 4 to 7
Release notes

Sourced from actions/upload-artifact's releases.

v7.0.0

v7 What's new

Direct Uploads

Adds support for uploading single files directly (unzipped). Callers can set the new archive parameter to false to skip zipping the file during upload. Right now, we only support single files. The action will fail if the glob passed resolves to multiple files. The name parameter is also ignored with this setting. Instead, the name of the artifact will be the name of the uploaded file.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

title: fix: separate execution modes and fix credential wiring
description:
## Summary

- **Fix credential Secret key mismatch**: Both credential paths (Keycloak and interactive) wrote K8s Secret keys that didn't match the env var names `config.py` reads. Renamed all keys to `VIP_TEST_USERNAME`, `VIP_TEST_PASSWORD`, `VIP_CONNECT_API_KEY`, `VIP_WORKBENCH_API_KEY`, `VIP_PM_TOKEN`.
- **Fix envFrom mount**: `create_job` conditionally skipped mounting the credentials Secret when `interactive_auth=True`, making interactive credentials invisible to the Job. Now always mounts the Secret. Removed the `interactive_auth` parameter.
- **Add Mode enum**: Introduced `Mode(str, Enum)` with `local`, `k8s_job`, `config_only` values and `VIPConfig.validate_for_mode()` that raises on missing required fields per mode.
- **Split run_verify**: Broke the monolithic function into `_resolve_mode`, `_phase_generate_config`, `_phase_provision_credentials`, `_phase_run_tests` with `run_verify` as a thin orchestrator.
- **Documentation**: Added mode/credential matrix to `vip.toml.example` and updated CLI help text.

## Test plan

- [x] All 75 selftests pass (`uv run pytest selftests/ -v`)
- [x] Ruff lint and format pass (`just check`)

title: ci: add semantic release with conventional commit enforcement
description:
## Summary

- Configure python-semantic-release for v0.x.x versioning (`major_on_zero = false`)
- Add `release.yml` workflow that runs on merge to main, using a deploy key to push tags (so `docker.yml` fires on `v*` tags)
- Add PR title check via `amannn/action-semantic-pull-request` to enforce conventional commits on squash merges
- Version is bumped in both `pyproject.toml` and `src/vip/__init__.py`

## Setup required before merge

1. ~~Generate a deploy key: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "vip-deploy-key" -f vip-deploy-key -N ""`~~
2. ~~Add the **public key** as a deploy key in repo Settings > Deploy keys (with write access)~~
3. ~~Add the **private key** as a secret named `DEPLOY_KEY` in repo Settings > Secrets > Actions~~

All done via CLI:
```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "vip-deploy-key" -f /tmp/vip-deploy-key -N ""
gh repo deploy-key add /tmp/vip-deploy-key.pub -R posit-dev/vip -t "semantic-release" -w
gh secret set DEPLOY_KEY -R posit-dev/vip < /tmp/vip-deploy-key
rm /tmp/vip-deploy-key /tmp/vip-deploy-key.pub
```

## Test plan

- [x] Create deploy key and add to repo
- [x] PR title check passes with conventional title (`ci: ...`)
- [ ] Merge PR and verify `release.yml` runs (should be a no-op since `ci:` type doesn't trigger a release)

title: Add vip verify and vip cluster CLI commands
description:
## Summary

Gene transfusion: PTD K8s access patterns → VIP. Makes VIP fully independent for cluster access and deployment verification.

### New commands

```bash
vip verify <target>                          # Full verification (K8s Job)
vip verify <target> --interactive-auth       # OIDC: browser login + token minting
vip verify <target> --local                  # Run tests locally
vip verify <target> --config-only            # Print generated vip.toml
vip verify cleanup <target>                  # Delete credentials + resources
vip cluster connect <target>                 # Generate kubeconfig only
```

### New modules

| Module | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `src/vip/cluster/aws.py` | AWS EKS kubeconfig via boto3 (STS presigned URL tokens) |
| `src/vip/cluster/azure.py` | Azure AKS kubeconfig via azure SDK |
| `src/vip/cluster/kubeconfig.py` | Cloud-agnostic kubeconfig writer |
| `src/vip/cluster/target.py` | Cluster config validation |
| `src/vip/verify/site.py` | Site CR → vip.toml generation |
| `src/vip/verify/credentials.py` | Keycloak + interactive auth provisioning |
| `src/vip/verify/job.py` | K8s Job creation, log streaming, cleanup |

### Live tested

Verified end-to-end against `ganso01-staging` (AWS EKS):
- EKS kubeconfig generation with cross-account role assumption ✓
- Site CR fetch + vip.toml generation ✓
- K8s Secret create/read/delete ✓
- K8s Job lifecycle (ConfigMap → Job → logs → cleanup) ✓
- CLI help and subcommands ✓

### Dependencies

Cloud SDKs are optional: `pip install vip[cluster]`

```toml
[cluster]
provider = "aws"
name = "ganso01-staging-20250328"
region = "us-east-2"
profile = "ptd-staging"
role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::654654567442:role/admin.posit.team"
```

vip verify <target>                          # Full verification (K8s Job)

title: Fix PM smoke tests: provision repos and handle unsynced repos gracefully
description:
Fresh Package Manager Docker containers start with zero repositories, causing `test_repo_exists` to hard-fail with `AssertionError: No repositories configured in Package Manager`.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/packagemanager-smoke.yml`**: Add a "Provision smoke test repositories" step between the health check and the test run. Uses `rspm` CLI inside the container to create CRAN and PyPI repos:

```bash
docker exec packagemanager /opt/rstudio-pm/bin/rspm create repo --name=cran-all --type=r
docker exec packagemanager /opt/rstudio-pm/bin/rspm create source --name=cran-mirror --type=cran-snapshot
docker exec packagemanager /opt/rstudio-pm/bin/rspm subscribe --repo=cran-all --source=cran-mirror

docker exec packagemanager /opt/rstudio-pm/bin/rspm create repo --name=pypi-all --type=python
# (no source subscription for PyPI — no proxy mirror source type exists in PPM)
```

- **`tests/package_manager/test_repos.py`**: Updated `query_cran` and `query_pypi` steps to call `pytest.skip` when a repo exists but its package endpoint is inaccessible (e.g. not yet synced), rather than returning `False` which causes the `then` step to hard-fail. This makes the smoke tests resilient to freshly provisioned repos that haven't completed a sync.

## Expected CI outcome

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_package_manager_reachable` | ✅ passes |
| `test_repo_exists` | ✅ passes (repos are provisioned) |
| `test_cran_mirror` | ✅ passes or ⏭️ skips (depends on whether `cran-snapshot` proxies on-demand) |
| `test_pypi_mirror` | ⏭️ skips (no PyPI source configured; no proxy source type in PPM) |

title: Handle OIDC/federated auth in `test_connect_login_ui` via `--interactive-auth`
description:
`test_connect_login_ui` unconditionally attempts to fill a username/password form on Connect's login page. When Connect uses an OIDC provider, the page redirects to the IdP — no such form exists — causing a 30-second `TimeoutError`.

## Changes

- **`src/vip/plugin.py`** — adds `--interactive-auth` CLI flag signaling that browser storage state is pre-loaded (user is already authenticated externally)
- **`tests/conftest.py`** — exposes `interactive_auth` as a session-scoped fixture
- **`tests/connect/test_auth.py`** — `enter_credentials` step now branches on `auth_provider`:
  - `"password"`: existing form-fill flow, unchanged
  - non-password + `--interactive-auth`: waits for the post-auth redirect (storage state already injected)
  - non-password without `--interactive-auth`: `pytest.skip` with a message directing the user to the flag
- **`selftests/test_plugin.py`** — adds integration test confirming `--interactive-auth` is registered and readable

```python
@when("enters valid credentials")
def enter_credentials(page, test_username, test_password, auth_provider, interactive_auth):
    if auth_provider != "password":
        if not interactive_auth:
            pytest.skip(
                f"Login form not available for auth provider {auth_provider!r}. "
                "Pass --interactive-auth when browser storage state is pre-loaded."
            )
        page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
        return
    page.fill("[name='username'], #username", test_username)
    ...
```

title: Add --interactive-auth for OIDC login
description:
## Summary
- Add `--interactive-auth` pytest flag that launches a headed browser for manual OIDC login before running tests
- After login, navigates the Connect UI to mint a temporary API key (`_vip_interactive`) so httpx-based API tests also work
- Captures browser storage state (cookies + localStorage) and injects it into all test browser contexts
- Cleans up: deletes the API key at session end, closes browser before tests start
- Automatically skips the credential prerequisite check when interactive auth is active

## How it works

1. User runs `uv run pytest --interactive-auth`
2. A visible Chromium window opens and navigates to Connect's `/__login__` endpoint
3. Connect redirects to the IdP (Okta, Azure AD, etc.)
4. User authenticates in the browser
5. VIP navigates to the Connect API Keys page and creates a temporary key via the UI
6. Browser storage state is saved, browser closes
7. Tests run headlessly — Playwright tests use the storage state, httpx API tests use the minted key
8. At session end, the API key is deleted via httpx

## Files changed

- **`src/vip/auth.py`** (new) — `InteractiveAuthSession` class, `start_interactive_auth()`, UI-based API key creation/deletion
- **`src/vip/plugin.py`** — Added `--interactive-auth` option, session lifecycle (create in `pytest_configure`, cleanup in `pytest_sessionfinish`)
- **`tests/conftest.py`** — `browser_context_args` override to inject storage state, `interactive_auth` fixture
- **`README.md`** — Authentication section documenting all auth modes

## Tested

Against `ganso01-staging` (Okta OIDC, Traefik forward-auth):

title: Implement stubbed package repository verification steps for Connect and Workbench
description:
Two test modules had all their step implementations stubbed with `pytest.skip("Not yet implemented")` and their scenarios decorated with `@pytest.mark.skip`, making them no-ops. This implements the actual verification logic for both.

## `tests/connect/test_packages.py`

Removes `@pytest.mark.skip` from both scenarios and implements the two `@then` steps:

- **`r_repo_present`** — checks known Connect field names (`r_repos_url`, `r_default_repo_url`, `repos_url`, `r_repos`) first; falls back to scanning all string leaf values for any HTTP URL via a recursive `_string_values()` helper; skips gracefully if nothing is found (older Connect versions may not expose this).
- **`pm_url_in_settings`** — walks all string values in the settings dict and requires the Package Manager URL to match exactly or as a URL prefix (`startswith(pm_base + "/")`), avoiding false positives from unrelated fields.

## `tests/workbench/test_packages.py`

Removes `@pytest.mark.skip` from the scenario and implements the two remaining steps:

- **`check_r_repos`** — uses the already-authenticated Playwright `page` to probe likely admin paths (`/admin/r`, `/admin/`, `/s/admin/r`, `/s/admin/`) and extracts HTTPS URLs from page content; skips with an informative message if none of the paths are accessible (e.g. non-admin test user).
- **`repo_url_present`** — matches the configured Package Manager URL against discovered URLs using exact equality or proper URL-prefix matching to avoid substring false positives:

```python
found = any(
    u.rstrip("/") == expected or u.startswith(expected + "/")
    for u in repo_check_url
)
```

title: Phase 2: Connect smoke test version matrix, test result artifacts, report preview, and job summaries
description:
Phase 1 established a minimal smoke test workflow against a single pinned Connect version. Phase 2 expands coverage by testing against multiple versions, makes failures debuggable, fixes the report preview, and adds rich CI visibility.

## Changes

### `connect-smoke.yml`
- **Version matrix** — runs smoke tests against both `2024.08.0` (pinned stable) and `release` (latest); `fail-fast: false` so both legs always run
- **Resolved version tracking** — after Connect starts, queries `/__api__/server_settings` to resolve `release` to its actual concrete version number (e.g. `2025.03.0`); logs the response body on failure for easier debugging
- **Dynamic job title** — uses `actions/github-script@v7` and the GitHub Checks API (`checks.update`) to rename the running check run from `Smoke test against Connect release` to `Smoke test against Connect 2025.03.0`, so the job list is always unambiguous
- **JUnit XML output** — adds `--junitxml=smoke-results.xml` to the pytest invocation
- **Test result artifact upload** — uploads per-version artifacts named with the resolved version (e.g. `connect-smoke-results-2025.03.0`) with `if: always()` for post-failure debugging
- **Rich workflow summary** — writes a `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` with emoji-formatted run metadata (requested version, resolved version, Connect URL, run date) and a parsed test results table (✅ Passed / ❌ Failed / ⚠️ Errors / ⏭️ Skipped / 📝 Total) with a 🎉 / 💥 status line

### `preview.yml`
- **Report preview fix** — spins up Connect via `with-connect`, resolves its actual version, generates a `vip.toml` pointing at that instance (including the `version` field), and runs the Connect smoke tests with `--vip-report` before rendering the Quarto report; the "Products Under Test" section now accurately shows Connect with its URL and concrete version instead of "No products configured" / "—"
- **Resolved version in deployment name** — the generated `vip.toml` sets `deployment_name = "CI Connect <version>"` so the report header also reflects the exact version tested

title: ci(workbench): derive [runtimes] and make test_packages real
description:
Closes #551. Partially addresses #550 — see the correction below.

## What changed

| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| `[runtimes]` derived from `/opt/R` and `/opt/python` | `test_runtime_versions` skipped on unset config (#550) |
| Non-version entries filtered out | Both dirs hold a `default` symlink; `/opt/python` also holds `jupyter` |
| Hard failure when enumeration is empty | An image-layout change would silently return the tests to skipping while looking fixed |
| `[package_manager]` URL, full tier only | Makes `test_packages` assert (#551) without putting PPM on the merge path |
| `test_packages` moved gate → full | It needs that URL, and on the gate it burned 29s then skipped |

## Measured results

Dispatch run `30404689341`, full tier:

```
Detected R: ["4.3.3","4.4.3"]
Detected Python: ["3.11.13","3.12.11"]

test_packages::test_r_repo_configured            PASSED
test_runtime_versions::test_r_version_in_session PASSED
test_runtime_versions::test_r_versions           SKIPPED — R version selector not present in New Session dialog
test_runtime_versions::test_python_versions      SKIPPED — Python version selector not present
```

## Correction to #550

I filed #550 claiming this was three tests of free coverage. It is one. The other two skip because the container's New Session dialog exposes no version selector — a UI affordance, not a config gap, and nothing `[runtimes]` can change. #550 should stay open or be re-scoped rather than closed by this PR.

Also worth being precise about what the passing test proves: `[runtimes]` is derived from the same container the test then checks, so it cannot catch "the wrong runtimes were installed". What it does catch is Workbench reporting a different version in-session than is installed on disk. That is a real check, narrower than the test name suggests.

## Local verification

The config script was executed directly for both tiers with a stubbed `docker`, rather than eyeballed:

- `gate` → no `[package_manager]` URL; `full` → URL present.
- Filtering drops `default` and `jupyter`.
- Empty enumeration emits `::error` and exits 1.
- VIP's own loader reads back `r_versions = ['4.3.3', '4.4.3']`, `python_versions = ['3.11.13', '3.12.11']`, `pm configured = True`.

`zizmor` reports 0 findings for the enforced audits.

## Unrelated failure in the verification run

The run's `release` leg failed, but not on anything here: `test_session_capacity` failed with `3/4 sessions reached Active. Failed profiles: Large`. That test passed in the #539 measurement and failed now — launching four sessions with resource profiles on a hosted runner looks resource-dependent. It is nightly-tier only, so it does not gate merges. Happy to file it.

title: fix(report): render out of the box after bare uv tool install
description:
Fixes #554.

## Problem

`vip report` failed after a plain `uv tool install posit-vip` for **two independent reasons**:

1. **Missing deps.** The report/Jupyter stack was only in the optional `[report]` extra, so a bare install had no `nbformat`/`nbclient`/`jupyter` in any environment Quarto could see. The cells in `report/details.qmd` / `report/index.qmd` couldn't run.
2. **Wrong interpreter.** `vip report` shells out to `quarto render`, and Quarto discovers its Jupyter kernel from the ambient `VIRTUAL_ENV` (set by `uv run` or an activated venv) or falls back to `/usr/bin/python3` — never `sys.executable`. So even with `[report]` installed into the tool venv, `uv run vip report` from another project grabbed *that project's* venv (→ `ModuleNotFoundError: vip.gherkin`), and plain `vip report` hit `/usr/bin/python3` (→ `ModuleNotFoundError: nbformat`).

Confirmed workaround that motivated the fix:
```bash
uv tool install --force 'posit-vip[report]'
QUARTO_PYTHON="$(uv tool dir)/posit-vip/bin/python" vip report --open   # renders cleanly
```

## Fix

1. **Fold the report/Jupyter deps into base `[project.dependencies]`** so any `posit-vip` install can render. `[report]` stays as an empty back-compat alias — `posit-vip[report]` still resolves, it just pulls the base deps.
2. **Pin `QUARTO_PYTHON=sys.executable`** in `run_report` when invoking `quarto render`, so the kernel is always the interpreter running `vip` (which, after #1, always has both `posit-vip` and the Jupyter stack). This also neutralises the `uv run` / `VIRTUAL_ENV` hijack.

Also: dropped the stale `pip install 'posit-vip[report]'` hint from the no-output error message.

## Verification

- Wheel `METADATA` now lists the Jupyter stack as unconditional `Requires-Dist` (not `extra == "report"`); `report` remains a `Provides-Extra` alias with nothing gated behind it.
- End-to-end `vip report` render succeeds from a scratch dir **with `VIRTUAL_ENV` deliberately pointed at an unrelated venv**, proving the `QUARTO_PYTHON` pin overrides the hijack.
- `just relock` regenerated `uv.lock` (also corrects a pre-existing `posit-vip 0.58.0 → 0.58.9` self-version drift already on `main`).
- Full selftest suite green (1155+), including a new test asserting the `QUARTO_PYTHON` pin survives a hostile `VIRTUAL_ENV`, plus updated dependency-pinning guards.

title: ci(connect): run the cross-product suite in a nightly tier
description:
Closes #540.

## What this covers

`cross_product/test_integration` was the last suite in #540 without CI coverage — the one that needs Connect and Package Manager both reachable.

## It did not need what I expected

I assumed a Package Manager container, Connect reconfigured to use it as its R repository, cross-container networking, and a CRAN snapshot synced before packages resolved. A measurement run showed all of that to be unnecessary: Connect's images already default their R repository at public PPM, so `test_connect_uses_package_manager` passes with nothing but the URL declared in config.

Measured PASSED on Connect `release`, `2026.06.0` and `2026.05.1`.

## Why it is nightly, not gated

Declaring `[package_manager]` has a side effect: `prerequisites/test_components.py` and `cross_product/test_resources.py` both health-check every configured product, so the gate would gain an explicit liveness check against `packagemanager.posit.co`. Measured, not theorised — the first run showed `test_product_server_is_reachable[Package Manager] PASSED` on what would have been a required check.

To be precise about the reasoning: the gate is **already** not hermetic. Connect's R deploys (`test_deploy_plumber`, `test_deploy_shiny`, `test_deploy_rmarkdown`) pull binaries from `packagemanager.posit.co`, `p3m.dev` and `rspm-sync.rstudio.com` on every single run. So this change is not preserving some pristine offline gate. What it avoids is *widening* that surface and, more importantly, adding a check whose only job is to assert an external service is up — an outage there would redden every PR while telling us nothing about this repo.

| Tier | Trigger | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `gate` | PR, push | Local container plus the package downloads Connect already performs |
| `full` | schedule, dispatch | Adds `cross_product/test_integration` and the `[package_manager]` config block |

Same shape as the `workbench-smoke.yml` split from #549, so there is one pattern to learn rather than two.

## Verification

- `full` tier dispatched: `test_connect_uses_package_manager PASSED`, 27 passed / 5 skipped in 74s.
- `gate` tier dispatched separately: neither `test_integration` nor the Package Manager health check appears, and the count returns to the 24-passed baseline.
- The config step's generated `vip.toml` was executed locally for both tiers and produces valid TOML, since a heredoc nested in an `if` is easy to get subtly wrong.
- `zizmor` reports 0 findings for the two enforced audits.

## Unrelated flake seen during verification

The `gate` verification run failed on its `2026.06.0` leg, and it is worth recording because it is not caused by this change. `test_deploy_plumber` and `test_deploy_shiny` failed when packrat could not fetch binaries:

```
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: Connection reset by peer in connection to rspm-sync.rstudio.com:443
Error in getSourceForPkgRecord(...) : Failed to download current version of fontawesome(0.5.3)
```

Both tests passed on the `release` and `2026.05.1` legs of the same run, so this is transient upstream CDN behaviour rather than a version-specific problem. It does mean the Connect gate can go red for reasons entirely outside this repository. Worth its own issue.

title: ci(workbench): split the Workbench suite into gate and nightly tiers
description:
Closes #539. Replaces #547, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted by the #545 merge; same two commits, cherry-picked onto current `main`.

## What the measurement found

A `suite=full` dispatch run across Workbench `release`, `2026.06.0` and `2026.05.1` — all three green. Per file, against a bare container:

| File | Passes | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `test_ide_extensions` | **3/3** | 83s — promoted to the gate |
| `test_git_ops` | 3/6 | clones pass; pushes skip, test repo is anonymous read-only |
| `test_session_capacity` | **1/1** | 74s |
| `test_jobs` | 1/2 | no Background Jobs tab in the container |
| `test_runtime_versions` | 0/3 | skips on unset `[runtimes]` — a config gap, not an infra one |
| `test_session_idle` | 0/2 | needs `idle_timeout_minutes`, then waits it out |
| `test_chronicle` | 0/1 | needs `[chronicle] enabled` |
| `test_sessions` | 0/1 | container does not support suspend/resume |
| `test_publish_to_connect` | deselected | Connect disabled in this workflow |

8 real passes for 523s. Total test time 718s versus 195s for the gate set.

## The split

- **gate** — PR and push. Adds `test_ide_extensions` only. Best ratio in the set and everything in this tier either passes or skips for a reason a Docker Workbench can never satisfy.
- **full** — nightly schedule, or `workflow_dispatch` on demand. Everything, so the slow suites are still exercised daily without taxing the merge path.

`test_session_capacity_k8s.py` is excluded from both: it needs a real Kubernetes launcher.

## Two findings worth separate action

1. **`test_runtime_versions` is free coverage being left on the floor.** All three tests skip on "No expected R versions specified in vip.toml `[runtimes]`". The workflow could populate `[runtimes]` from the running container and convert 3 skips into 3 real assertions. Noted in the workflow; happy to file it.
2. **`test_packages` is already on the gate and always skips** — "Package Manager URL is not configured in vip.toml". It burns 29s for zero coverage on every gated run. Either give the Workbench job a PM URL or drop the file from the gate.

## Verification

The measured run is the verification: run `30388705167`, all three versions green, 18 passed / 13 skipped / 6 deselected. `zizmor` reports 0 findings for the enforced audits and the workflow parses. `AGENTS.md` documents the tiers and the fact that skip reasons only appear in the XML artifact.

title: fix(workbench): clarify password-login skip on SSO deployments
description:
## Summary

The skip message for the Workbench password-login scenario on an SSO/OIDC deployment advised passing `--interactive-auth`/`--headless-auth`. That advice is misleading for this specific scenario.

`test_workbench_login`'s `page` fixture deliberately strips the pre-loaded `storage_state` (`test_auth.py:49`) so it exercises a genuine logged-out password form, and its step calls `workbench_login(...)` without threading `interactive_auth`/`auth_mode` (`test_auth.py:82`). So those flags cannot make this scenario run — a user who has *already* passed `--interactive-auth` still hits this skip and gets told to pass a flag they just passed.

## Change

Reword the skip at `conftest.py:587` to:
- lead with what the test needs (a password-login form),
- name the tell (no username/password fields),
- drop the inapplicable `--interactive-auth`/`--headless-auth` advice.

**Before:**
> Workbench is configured for SSO/OIDC (no password login form); the password-login scenario does not apply. Pass --interactive-auth or --headless-auth to exercise authenticated Workbench tests.

**After:**
> This scenario requires a Workbench password-login form, but the deployment presents an SSO/OIDC sign-in page instead (no username/password fields). Password login cannot be exercised on an SSO deployment, so this scenario is skipped.

The other two skips in this path still route through `_workbench_session_skip_message(...)`, which correctly names those flags for the paths that honor a pre-loaded session — those are left unchanged.

## Testing

- `ruff check` passes on the changed file.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: ci(workbench): split the Workbench suite into gate and nightly tiers
description:
Closes #539. Stacked on #545 — merge that first.

## What the measurement found

A `suite=full` dispatch run across Workbench `release`, `2026.06.0` and `2026.05.1` — all three green. Per file, against a bare container:

title: ci(smoke): run cross-cutting suites and stop writing secrets to disk
description:
Part of #540. First increment; the remaining pieces are noted at the bottom.

## Coverage added

| Suite | Connect | Workbench | Package Manager |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cross_product/test_resources` | yes | yes | yes |
| `security/test_auth_policy` | yes (both scenarios) | provider check only | — |
| `config_hygiene/test_secrets` | yes (both scenarios) | no-plaintext check | no-plaintext check |

Connect gains 5 tests, Workbench 3, Package Manager 2. The Connect-dependent scenarios are deselected automatically where Connect is not enabled, so nothing skips silently on a technicality.

## The security fix this surfaced

Adding `config_hygiene/test_secrets` failed immediately, for a good reason: every smoke workflow was writing a live credential into `vip.toml` on the runner.

- `connect-smoke.yml` wrote `api_key = "<with-connect bootstrap key>"`
- `workbench-smoke.yml` wrote `password = "<container password>"`

`config.py` already supports env-var fallbacks (`VIP_CONNECT_API_KEY` at line 89, `VIP_TEST_PASSWORD` at line 354), so the fix needed no product-code change — pass them as step `env` and stop writing them to the file.

Verified in both directions locally, since `test_secrets` only reads the config file:

```
OLD Connect config:    test_no_plaintext_secrets FAILED — Plaintext secrets found: ['api_key']
OLD Workbench config:  test_no_plaintext_secrets FAILED — Plaintext secrets found: ['password']
NEW Connect config:    2 passed
NEW Workbench config:  1 passed, 1 deselected
```

That is the point of the test, and it was catching something real on its first run.

## Removing `-k "workbench"`

`workbench-smoke.yml` filtered with `-k "workbench"`. Collection is byte-identical without it — the plugin already deselects scenarios for products that are not enabled in `vip.toml`, which is what that filter was standing in for. Left in place, it would have silently deselected all three new suites, since none of their test names contain "workbench".

## Verification

All three workflows are change-gated on their own path, so opening this PR runs all three against real containers — that is the actual verification and I will report the result. Locally: `zizmor` reports 0 findings for the two enforced audits, all three workflows parse, and collection was checked against the exact configs each workflow now generates.

## Still open on #540

- `cross_product/test_integration` needs Connect and Package Manager in the same job — a new workflow, next increment.
- `security/test_https` and `cross_product/test_ssl` skip unless the URL is HTTPS, so they need a TLS front-end. Being split into its own issue rather than deferred silently.
- `cross_product/test_monitoring` is gone — removed by #543, so the issue body needs correcting.

title: ci: add CI Status aggregator and document the integration gate
description:
Part of #421. Covers the two remaining code-side items; the ruleset changes are admin actions listed below.

## CI Status aggregator

`Type Check`, `Actions Lint (zizmor)`, `Dependency Audit` and `Lockfile Guard` all run on every relevant PR but none of them gates a merge — the required-check set is `Lint & Format`, `Selftests Status`, `check-title` and the three product-smoke Status jobs. A red `Dependency Audit` does not block anything today.

They cannot simply be added to the ruleset: all four are conditional on the `changes` job, so a `changes` failure skips every dependent, and skipped required checks count as passing. That is the exact hole `Selftests Status` was built to close, so `CI Status` copies it.

Behaviour, unit-tested against all five result combinations before pushing:

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| All four succeed | pass |
| Docs-only PR (all skipped) | pass |
| Push to main (Lockfile Guard skipped by design) | pass |
| Any job fails | fail, with the job named in a `::error::` annotation |
| Any job cancelled | fail |
| `changes` itself fails | fail before evaluating anything |

## connect-integration.yml stays scheduled-only

#421 asked to either promote it or record why not. Recording why not: the matrix includes `preview`, the Connect nightly build, so a required check there would let an unreleased upstream regression block every VIP merge. `connect-smoke.yml` already gates the Connect path on PRs. The reasoning now lives in the workflow header rather than only in the issue.

## Follow-up admin actions

`CI Status` does nothing until it is in the ruleset. After this merges, add both it and `Mock-IdP E2E Status` to `repos/posit-dev/vip/rulesets/12514854`.

## Verification

`zizmor` with the repo config reports 0 findings for the two enforced audits (`unpinned-uses`, `artipacked`) — the same gate `Actions Lint` applies. Both workflows parse. `AGENTS.md` updated to describe the new required check.

title: test: remove duplicative monitoring health-check test
description:
## What

Removes `cross_product/test_monitoring.py` and its `test_monitoring.feature`.

## Why

`test_monitoring_configured` probed the same three product liveness endpoints already covered elsewhere, so it added no coverage:

| Test | Assertion | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `prerequisites/test_components` | `status < 400` | per-product reachability |
| `cross_product/test_resources` (Product server health) | `status == 200` | aggregate, follows redirects, richer failure output |
| `cross_product/test_monitoring` *(removed)* | `status < 400` | aggregate, weaker, no redirect handling |

Two problems with the removed test:

1. **Duplicative.** Its probe was a strict subset of `test_resources` — same endpoints (`/__api__/server_settings`, `/health-check`, `/__api__/status`), weaker check, less diagnostic output.
2. **Mislabeled.** Its "Monitoring and logging" feature framing promised verification that monitoring/logging is *configured*, but the implementation checked none of that — only process liveness. Posit products don't expose Prometheus-style metrics over the standard HTTP API (see the note in `test_resources.py`), so a genuine monitoring check would require a metrics-proxy extension, not this.

### How the bug surfaced

The test was gated behind `[monitoring] enabled = false` (off by default), so it rarely ran. When monitoring was enabled during a real deployment run, it failed with a Connect **HTTP 404**: it uniquely used `/__api__/v1/server_settings`, but `server_settings` is not under the `v1` namespace — the correct path (used by every other caller and the client) is `/__api__/server_settings`. Rather than fix a stale path in a test no coverage depends on, this removes the dead duplicate.

## Scope

The `monitoring_enabled` config flag is intentionally **left in place** — it's a documented `vip.toml` surface and removing it would be a breaking config change. It's now unused by tests; a follow-up can decide whether to repurpose it for a real monitoring check or deprecate it.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest selftests/ -q` → 1155 passed
- No dangling references to the removed scenario across `src/`, `selftests/`, `examples/`, `report/`

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(auth): refresh the cached session after restoring a signed-out one
description:
`test_workbench_signout` ends the shared Workbench session and `restore_shared_session` (added in #574) mints a fresh one — but only in the browser context. The cache on disk kept the cookies the sign-out killed, so every subsequent `vip verify` probed that cache, found it dead, and dropped into an interactive re-auth, opening a browser at the user on every single run.

## Approach

A successful restore writes the context's storage state back over the cache, via `refresh_auth_cache_from_storage_state` in `src/vip/auth.py` — which already owns `auth_cache_path()` and the cache format, so that knowledge stays in one place.

Four decisions worth reviewing:

- **Only refreshes a cache that already exists.** Absent means no `--interactive-auth` run put one there (a password deployment, say); creating one would leave a storage state with no companion `.meta.json` for `_load_cached_auth` to match URLs against.
- **Atomic and owner-only.** `mkstemp` in the same directory then `os.replace`, so a concurrent xdist worker never reads a half-written file, and the replacement keeps `0600` — it holds live session cookies.
- **A cache failure does not fail the restore.** `_refresh_cached_session` always returns `True`: an unwritable cache is a slower next run, not a failed restore, and reporting it as one would trip the loud warning meant for a genuinely signed-out suite.
- **`.meta.json` is left untouched** — API key and URLs are unrelated to session liveness. Asserted by a selftest.

## Live verification

Against Workbench 2026.06.0 behind Okta. Cache liveness probed read-only, no browser, via `_cached_workbench_session_is_live`.

**Before** — cache written by a fully passing run, checked 16 minutes later with only the sign-out in between:

```
is_live: False
detail : the request landed on the sign-in page at https://dev.current.posit.team/auth-sign-in?appUri=%2F
```

**After** — same probe, right after a sign-out run on this branch:

```
is_live   : True
detail    : (dashboard reached)
cache age : 50s
cache mode: 0o600
temp files left behind: none
```

And the next run reuses it instead of opening a browser:

```
>>> Reusing cached auth session from /Users/ianfloressiaca/.vip-auth-cache.json
1 passed, 1 skipped, 140 deselected in 0.46s
```

## Scope

This covers the sign-out path, the one place we hold a live context at the moment the session rotates. If the cache proves to die for other reasons (Workbench rotating cookies on login, an idle timeout), the general fix is to refresh at end of run rather than only after sign-out. The evidence points at sign-out, so this stays narrow.

Selftests cover the rewrite, permission preservation, refusing to create an absent cache, leaving no temp file behind, a non-serialisable state leaving the cache intact, and both restore paths. 1423 passed across three randomized runs; the 2 intermittent failures are the pre-existing flaky threadpool tests (#517), which fail identically on clean main. Ruff and mypy clean.

title: ci: adopt calendar versioning on a weekly release train
description:
## What

Replaces semver-on-every-merge with calendar versioning on a scheduled weekly train. The first release under this scheme is `2026.7.0`, superseding `0.58.x`, and retires the planned 1.0 cutover along with the `major_on_zero = false` workaround that existed to prevent it.

## The cadence is one rule

"First Thursday of the month cuts the monthly release, other Thursdays cut patches" needs no nth-weekday logic (cron cannot express it) and no day-of-month arithmetic. It reduces to *is this the first release of this calendar month?* — because the first Thursday of a month is necessarily that month's first release.

| last tag | today | next |
|---|---|---|
| `v2026.7.0` | 2026-07-30 | `2026.7.1` |
| `v2026.7.3` | 2026-08-06 | `2026.8.0` |
| `v2026.12.2` | 2027-01-07 | `2027.1.0` |
| `v2026.7.1` | 2026-09-03 | `2026.9.0` |
| `v0.58.17` | 2026-07-30 | `2026.7.0` |

Year rollover, skipped months, and the `0.x` cutover all fall out of the same branch with no special cases. `scripts/next_version.py` implements it; `selftests/test_next_version.py` covers each case, since every failure mode here is annual or rarer and would otherwise be found in production.

## Versions are unpadded, deliberately

PEP 440 strips leading zeros: `2026.07.0` normalizes to `2026.7.0`. Posit's zero-padded product style is a display convention a PyPI package cannot hold, so rather than carry two strings per release the version is unpadded everywhere, tag included. That also keeps it valid semver, which two existing pieces of machinery need: `docker.yml`'s `type=semver,pattern={{version}}` (leading zeros are invalid semver, so a padded tag would be silently skipped) and `publish.yml`'s `pip install "posit-vip==${VERSION}"` check (a padded tag would chase a version PyPI never publishes).

October through December read identically to Posit product style either way.

## python-semantic-release is removed entirely

PSR cannot be handed an explicit version — `semantic-release version` offers only `--major/--minor/--patch/--prerelease/--build-metadata`. Forcing flags nearly works if year is treated as major and month as minor, but `--major` on `2026.12.2` gives `2027.0.0` rather than `2027.1.0`, so every January would need a hand-fix.

Keeping PSR for changelog generation alone does not work either: its changelog is tag-driven and can only write an entry for a tag that already exists, which puts the changelog in a commit *after* the tag. `git-cliff --tag v<version>` sets the tag for a version that does not exist yet, so the entry lands inside the release commit, before the tag. `cliff.toml` reproduces the existing `CHANGELOG.md` layout; verified against a full-history regeneration of all 148 releases.

## Release gate

Any commit since the last tag ships. Commit types no longer influence the version at all — they still drive changelog grouping and are still enforced by `pr-title.yml`. This is deliberate: `chore` and `ci` are half of all merges (16 fix / 16 chore / 10 ci / 2 test since `v0.58.0`), so a PSR-style type gate would leave a week of dependency bumps unreleased.

## Notes for review

- **Issue #559 is preserved.** `build_command = "just relock"` and `assets = ["uv.lock"]` were the fix for it and lived in the config being deleted. Both are now explicit workflow steps — the relock step and `uv.lock` in the release commit's `git add`. Dropping either regresses #559, so both carry comments saying so.
- **`git push --atomic` is load-bearing.** Without it git updates refs independently, so a merge landing mid-run rejects the branch push while the tag still lands — and `publish.yml` triggers on tag push, publishing a release commit that is not on main. PyPI versions cannot be reused, so that state is unrecoverable.
- **`cliff.toml`'s header is coupled to the top of `CHANGELOG.md`.** `git-cliff --prepend` only strips the existing header when the configured `header` byte-matches; otherwise the file grows a second `# CHANGELOG` title. `selftests/test_changelog_header.py` asserts the prefix relation so drift fails a test rather than surfacing in a release commit after the tag is cut.
- **`workflow_dispatch` with no input is a "release now" button**, not an override — it keeps the no-commits gate. Only an explicit `version` bypasses that gate, and it still refuses anything not strictly greater than the last tag.
- All `${{ }}` values reaching shell are routed through `env:`, matching the existing `SUITE:` pattern in `workbench-smoke.yml`. zizmor flagged three high-confidence template-injection findings on the `inputs.version` interpolations before this.
- `publish.yml` needs no changes; it already triggers on `v*` tag push and is decoupled from how the tag is produced.

## Effect on merge

Merging stops automatic per-merge releases immediately. The next release is cut by the Thursday cron at 22:17 UTC, or on demand via `workflow_dispatch`.

## Testing

- `selftests/test_next_version.py` — 11 cases, passing.
- `selftests/test_changelog_header.py` — header/changelog coupling guard; verified it fails on a one-word drift.
- Full selftests: 1416 passed, 3 skipped. Two pre-existing `test_load_engine.py` failures are unrelated and tracked in #575.
- `just check` clean. `release.yml` parses; zizmor reports 0 findings in it and 0 for both CI-enforced audits.
- `next_version.py` against real tags and today's date → `2026.7.0`.
- `git-cliff --tag v2026.7.0 --unreleased --prepend` against a copy of the real `CHANGELOG.md` → single title, correct new section.

title: fix(cli): disambiguate vip version output labels
description:
## What

`vip version` now labels each of its two lines explicitly:

    VIP version: 0.58.13
    Supported Posit Team versions: 2026.04.0 and newer

Previously:

    vip 0.58.13
    Minimum supported Posit Team version: 2026.04.0

## Why

VIP is moving its own version numbering to calendar versioning, so its version will start to look like `2026.7.0` — the same shape as a Posit Team product version. The old output put an unlabeled VIP version directly above a Posit Team version, which reads as "this is the VIP for Posit Team 2026.07". The two numbers are unrelated: VIP's version says nothing about which product release it targets, and the support floor is a separate, independently maintained value.

Labeling both lines removes the ambiguity before the version format change lands and makes it hard to misread.

## Scope

The `--version` flag is deliberately unchanged. It still prints the conventional `vip <version>` and nothing else, since tooling may parse it.

`docker.yml`'s `docker run --rm "$ref" version` sanity check is a bare exit-code invocation with no output matching, so it is unaffected.

## Testing

`selftests/test_cli_version.py` previously asserted loose substrings. It now asserts the exact output string, so any future wording drift fails the test rather than passing silently.

title: fix(workbench): run sign-out last and restore the shared session
description:
`test_workbench_signout` ends the session every other Workbench scenario shares: under `--interactive-auth` / `--headless-auth` they all authenticate as one account. It inherited the module's `order(10)` — the earliest mark in the whole Workbench suite — so the one scenario that signs the shared account out ran before nearly everything else, while sibling xdist workers were mid-test.

Order it last (95) and have it hand the session back via a silent SSO round-trip in teardown. When that round-trip cannot complete (e.g. the IdP applied single-logout) it warns loudly rather than leaving the suite and the on-disk auth cache silently signed out.

Both scenarios now carry explicit order marks instead of one inheriting a module-level `pytestmark`: stacking a per-function mark on a module mark leaves the winner up to pytest-order's mark resolution.

## Evidence

A cached auth session minted at the start of a 2-test run was already dead 5 minutes later — the only session-affecting test in that window being the sign-out. Probed read-only, no browser:

```
is_live: False
detail : the request landed on the sign-in page at https://dev.current.posit.team/auth-sign-in?appUri=%2F
```

Honest caveat: this is not proven deterministic. An earlier cache *did* survive a run containing a passing sign-out. Either way the scenario mutates shared state and should restore it.

Ordering verified at collection against a configured Workbench: `test_workbench_login` collects first (item 1), `test_workbench_signout` last (item 33 of 33), after `test_ide_extensions`.

## Still to verify live

Whether silent SSO can re-establish after a Workbench sign-out, or whether the IdP applies single-logout and forces a full interactive login. In the latter case the teardown warns rather than repairs — better than silent breakage, but worth knowing. **Do not merge before that is checked.**

Selftests cover both restore outcomes and both ordering invariants: 1315 passed, the 2 failures being the pre-existing flaky threadpool tests (#517) which fail identically on clean main. Ruff and mypy clean.

title: fix(workbench): detect sign-in redirected to an external IdP
description:
`workbench_login` decided "password vs SSO" purely from markup on the page it landed on: a `#username` field, or a button named `/sign in/i`. A deployment that redirects unauthenticated requests straight to its IdP has neither — Okta's identifier-first submit is named "Next" — so the SSO branch never fired and the password retry loop ran to exhaustion, failing with `Login failed after 3 attempts` instead of skipping. Closes #375.

Landing off the Workbench origin is now conclusive on its own: no Workbench password form is reachable from an IdP's own domain, whatever that IdP's markup looks like. The skip messages name the IdP host so the reader isn't hunting for a Workbench sign-in page that was never rendered.

Also guards a latent crash: on the off-origin path the `--interactive-auth` branch would have clicked a locator resolving to nothing, raising a Playwright error in place of an actionable skip.

## How this was diagnosed

Probing the live sign-in page unauthenticated shows the redirect leaves Workbench entirely:

```
URL: https://posit.okta.com/oauth2/v1/authorize?client_id=...&response_type=code&scope=openid+profile+email
has #username: 0
role=button 'sign in': 0
role=link 'sign in': 0
```

Okta's submit is `button "Next"`, which is why every markup probe missed.

## Verification

Live Workbench 2026.06.0 behind Okta:

```
test_workbench_login   SKIPPED (This scenario requires a Workbench password-login form, but the
                       deployment redirects sign-in to the identity provider at posit.okta.com...)
test_workbench_signout PASSED
```

Selftests add an `_ExternalIdpFakePage` covering both the password and `--interactive-auth` paths, plus a `_PasswordLoginFakePage` regression test proving genuine password deployments still fill the form — the detection must not swallow those. 1313 passed; the 2 failures are the pre-existing flaky threadpool tests (#517), which fail identically on clean main. Ruff and mypy clean.

title: fix(workbench): scope session cleanup to the creating xdist worker
description:
The per-test cleanup fixture matched sessions on a bare `VIP ` prefix, so finishing a test on one xdist worker quit sessions another worker was still driving. That surfaced as vanished session rows, "Abnormal exits" toasts, a `Session status: Quit` banner inside a live VS Code session, and `jsonrpc error 1 (Unable to connect to service)` in an RStudio console — all of which read as deployment faults rather than a test-suite bug.

Session names already carried the creating worker id; nothing parsed it back out. `session_owner` / `is_vip_session_for_owner` now do, and every sweep that runs during a test run passes its own worker id. `vip cleanup --workbench-url` still sweeps globally, since it runs when no worker is left to disturb — that remains the path that clears orphans from a crashed worker or an older VIP release. Capacity sessions gained a worker segment (`_vip_cap_<worker>_<ts>_`) so they can be attributed too.

## Verification

Live Workbench 2026.06.0 deployment, 2 workers, same `vip verify --workbench-url … --interactive-auth` command each time:

| Run | Failed | Passed | Skipped | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (0.58.12) | 12 | 11 | 18 | 735s |
| this branch | 2 | 17 | 22 | 527s |

Newly passing: all three `test_ide_extensions` scenarios, `test_clone_rstudio`, `test_clone_positron`, `test_launch_vscode`, `test_launch_jupyter`, `test_session_suspend_resume`, `test_workbench_job`, `test_launch_sessions_with_the_configured_resource_profile`.

The 2 remaining failures are unrelated root causes, each getting its own PR: `test_workbench_login` (#375) and a `terminal_run` readback timeout in `test_clone_vscode` (the #390 family).

Selftests: 1324 passed. The 2 failures are the pre-existing flaky threadpool tests (#517), which fail identically on clean main. Ruff and mypy clean.

## Note for reviewers

A per-test sweep no longer clears sessions it cannot attribute — orphans from a crashed worker, or from a VIP old enough that its names carry no worker segment. That is deliberate: during a run there is no safe way to tell those apart from a sibling worker's live session. `vip cleanup --workbench-url` remains the global sweep. If either naming format changes, `_VIP_OWNER_PATTERNS` in `src/vip/clients/workbench.py` must change with it; AGENTS.md now documents that contract.

title: fix: correct false skips, flaky search waits, and the header check
description:
## What

Three checks in `vip verify --package-manager-url` reported results that were not true. Found while investigating a run against a live 2026.06.0 deployment.

| Check | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `test_pypi_mirror` | falsely SKIPPED | PASSED |
| `test_package_search/detail[PyPI]` | intermittently FAILED | PASSED, warns when slow |
| `test_product_does_not_expose_sensitive_headers` | always FAILED | PASSED with a warning |

Against the same deployment: **1 failed / 22 passed / 9 skipped → 24 passed / 8 skipped / 1 warning**, with the control run taken on untouched `main` immediately beforehand.

## Repository selection

`test_repos.py` picked `repos[0]` from the name-matched candidates, making the outcome depend on the order the server happened to list them in. A `_first_repo_serving()` walk now backs all four ecosystems — the shape `query_openvsx` already had — and the skip reason names every repo tried.

## Search timeout

Package search against a full mirror is not comparable to the other UI waits, so it gets its own ceiling rather than a bump to the shared one. The 90s figure is measured, not guessed: eleven of twelve runs at ~4s, one at 53.8s on the session's first search, `cran` at ~1s throughout. Raising the ceiling alone would trade a false failure for a silent one, so `wait_for_search_results()` warns past 15s and fails with a readable diagnosis instead of a raw `Locator.wait_for: Timeout exceeded`.

## Header check

`server` is warned about, `x-powered-by` still fails. Splitting them is deliberate: a check where every branch warns can never fail, which is the failure mode #555 exists to remove. The scenario and step are renamed to match what they now assert.

## Tests

Two new selftest files (28 cases) plus header coverage in `test_https_helper.py`, which had none. The regression tests were confirmed to go red against the old behaviour, and the timeout constant was mutation-tested — the first draft of the repo-selection tests passed spuriously because the step's `pytest.skip` marked the *selftest* skipped rather than failed.

`docs/test-architecture.md` gains a fail/warn/skip section, since that distinction is now load-bearing.

Full suite green: ruff, format, mypy, 1321 selftests. (`test_load_engine.py` has a flaky timing assertion that fails on untouched `main` too.)

title: fix(auth): validate cached auth sessions and unify the cache path
description:
No linked issue — this came out of a Local Launcher run where all 106 collected tests reported skipped, initially read as a parallelism regression. It is not one.

## The two defects

A cached auth session in `.vip-auth-cache.json` was trusted on nothing but a four-hour mtime TTL. Nothing on the cache-hit path verified the saved browser session still worked, and `_authenticate_workbench` only runs on the *fresh*-auth path — so `workbench_auth_error` stayed `None`. A dead IdP session (expiry, an admin revoking it, a password change) therefore made every Workbench test skip through `_workbench_session_skip_message`, with a message that named no cause and told the user to rerun with `--vip-verbose`. The absence of the `Pre-test auth reported:` line in that skip text is the diagnostic tell for this path.

Separately, `vip verify` and `vip cleanup --workbench-url` read different cache files. `plugin.py` built the path from `Path(config.rootpath)` while `cli.py` used `Path.cwd()`, and cli.py's comment asserted the two matched. For an installed VIP (`uv tool install posit-vip`) the test paths live in site-packages, so pytest derives rootdir from the common ancestor of the invocation directory and site-packages — which lands in `$HOME`. The cache went nowhere near the user's `vip.toml`, and `cleanup` looked somewhere `verify` never wrote.

## Why the probe has three outcomes, not two

`_cached_workbench_session_is_live` returns `True`, `False`, or `None`, and the third value is load-bearing. `False` requires positive evidence that the session is dead: a redirect landing on the sign-in page, or a bare 401/403 for the configs that answer an expired session without redirecting. A transport error returns `None` and the cache is reused.

Treating an unreachable deployment as a dead session would be actively worse than the bug being fixed. It would discard a good cache, trigger an interactive re-auth that cannot succeed either because the server is down, and bury the real reachability error behind an auth-shaped one. `None` preserves exactly the pre-probe behaviour, so the tests report the outage with their own message.

The probe runs over plain httpx with cookies read out of the Playwright storage state, so there is no browser launch. Those cookies keep their domain and path, and go into an `httpx.Cookies` jar so httpx applies ordinary cookie matching. That scoping is not hygiene: the storage state spans a whole browser context including the IdP, so flattening it to `name -> value` would both leak the IdP's session cookie to the Workbench host and let two hosts sharing a cookie name overwrite each other — and sending the IdP's value for a name Workbench also uses would make a live session read as dead, causing the very re-auth this PR removes. It fires only when Workbench is requested, and only after the existing URL-match check, so Connect-only runs pay nothing. TLS settings thread through the existing `_httpx_verify`, so `--insecure` and `--ca-bundle` deployments are not failed on TLS and sent through a pointless re-auth. A malformed cache file yields no cookies rather than raising before any test executes.

## Why cwd, not rootpath

`auth_cache_path()` is now the single source of truth and both call sites use it. Keying on the invocation directory rather than rootdir makes the code match what its own docstring already claimed — one slot per checkout directory. For a repo checkout the two were always identical; rootdir only diverges for installed VIP, which is the case that broke. A selftest enforces the invariant by asserting neither `plugin.py` nor `cli.py` contains the filename literal, since that inline duplication is how the two drifted apart.

This orphans any existing cache under `$HOME`, costing one re-auth. The orphaned file is `0600` and holds a Connect API key.

## Verification

18 new selftests: cookie extraction including malformed and nameless-cookie input, each probe verdict including the inconclusive path and the 401/403 pair, the cache-miss wiring including Connect-only skipping the probe and TLS settings reaching it, the path helper and its invariant, and two end-to-end tests asserting a dead cache actually reaches the browser flow while a live one short-circuits it.

1302 selftests pass, `just check` clean, mypy clean across 29 files. The only failures are the two known macOS timing flakes in `test_load_engine.py`, reproduced on a stashed unmodified tree.

## Deliberately not fixed

The probe validates Workbench only. A revoked cached *Connect API key* has the same failure shape and is still trusted unvalidated.
